While melatonin has a role in the management of pediatric insomnia as well as of circadian rhythm disorders, the existing literature supports behavioral interventions as the first-line treatment option. Potential pitfalls in the clinical use of melatonin in children are important to recognize and incorporate into best-practice recommendations.

papers.title: Determination of changes in the nutrition and physical activity status of academicians during the pandemic period.
papers.abstract: To assess the changes in nutrition habits, physical activity levels, sedentary behaviours, sleep patterns and quality of academicians before and during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic. The descriptive, cross-sectional study was conducted from January to September 2022 after approval from Karadeniz Technical University, Turkiye, and comprised academicians working at public universities in Turkiye during the coronavirus disease-2019 pandemic period. The survey questionnaire was distributed online to all public universities across the country. The participants' food consumption before and during the epidemic, sleep patterns and physical activity conditions were assessed. Data was analysed using SPSS 22. Of the 299 academicians,166(55.5%) were female and 133(45.5%) were male. Overall age range was 19-65 years, with 122(40.8%) subjects aged 35-44 years. A significant number of academicians 143(47.83%) reported changes in their eating habits, while even more 189(64.29%) indicated that a sedentary lifestyle had a negative impact on their health. There was a significant increase in the number of snacks (p<0.001). A total of 125(42.09%) participants reported using nutritional supplements during the pandemic, with vitamins, multivitamins and minerals being the most commonly chosen options. A significant majority of participants 178(59.73%) reported changes in sleep patterns and weight-gain during the pandemic. The time spent watching TV and using computers, tablets and phones increased significantly during the isolation period (p<0.05). Also, there was a decrease in the physical activities of the academicians (p<0.05). Even within more aware segments of the population, such as academicians, the coronavirus disease- 2019 pandemic's impact on psychological wellbeing led to significant alterations in eating, sleeping and physical activity patterns.
papers.journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
keywords: COVID-19, Physical activity, Sleep, Feeding behaviour, Nutrition.

papers.title: Ambipolar Fiber Amplifiers for Highly Sensitive Biosignal Detection.
papers.abstract: Biological signals are inherently weak and susceptible to noise, making in situ signal amplification critical for high-fidelity sensing. Electronic fibers offer unique advantages for conformal and scalable biointegration; however, fiber amplifiers are seldom reported due to the lack of suitable semiconducting materials that combine balanced ambipolar transport, scalable fiber fabrication, and high device performance. Herein, we report the first single-component ambipolar fiber platform based on a newly designed polymer, P(gTDPP-TQ), which combines balanced p- and n-type transport, low-cost synthesis, and continuous fiber fabrication. Fiber processing enhances molecular ordering and charge transport, yielding record-high µC* and gm,norm among reported semiconducting fibers, enabling high-performance fiber amplifiers with a high voltage gain of up to 150 V V-1 and low operating voltages down to 0.5 V. These fiber amplifiers enable high-fidelity electroencephalogram signal amplification over 20 times and sensitive cortisol sensing with a record-low detection limit of 3.7 fM. This work establishes a general ambipolar fiber platform for integrated bioelectronic amplification and sensing.

papers.title: Burnout and Related Occupational and Psychological Outcomes Among Emergency Nurses in Saudi Arabia: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: To map primary Saudi studies reporting burnout, occupational fatigue, anxiety, depression, psychological distress, or sleep disturbance among emergency-department (ED) nurses. Scoping review. Following PRISMA-ScR, PubMed/MEDLINE, CINAHL Complete, ProQuest Nursing & Allied Health and Web of Science Core Collection were searched on 15 September 2026 using PCC-based controlled vocabulary and free-text terms. Primary quantitative, qualitative and mixed-methods studies (1 January 2015-15 September 2026) that meet the inclusion criteria were eligible. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data using a standardized form, resolving disagreements by discussion. Charted data covered design, setting, sample and ED-nurse denominator, outcome construct and instrument, scoring, nurse-specific results and associations. Synthesis was descriptive and grouped by construct; meta-analysis was not planned given heterogeneity in constructs, measures, thresholds and reporting. The four sources yielded 1694 raw record instances; 15 Saudi ED-nurse records were included. Seven quantitative reports measured burnout, while two qualitative studies described burnout-related experiences. Other records examined fatigue, anxiety/depression, occupational stress, or secondary traumatic stress. Variation in measures, thresholds, sampling and reporting precluded meta-analysis or a defensible pooled estimate. Evidence from selected Saudi emergency settings signals concerns across burnout and related outcomes, but limited geographic coverage and predominantly cross-sectional designs preclude national prevalence or causal conclusions. Distinguishing burnout from adjacent constructs is essential. Nursing leaders should monitor constructs separately using validated tools and ED-nurse-specific denominators, and pair confidential support with organizational action on modifiable work conditions. Future multisite longitudinal and intervention studies should assess feasibility and outcomes before wider adoption.

papers.title: SERPINE1 Identifies a Shared Injury-associated Molecular Signature in Intracerebral Hemorrhage and Epilepsy.
papers.abstract: Intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) and epilepsy are clinically linked neurological disorders, yet their shared molecular features remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular candidates across ICH and epilepsy by integrating transcriptomic data with a curated set of genes with established circadian relevance. Transcriptomic datasets for ICH and epilepsy were retrieved from the Gene Expression Omnibus, and candidate genes were curated from the Molecular Signatures Database and GeneCards. Differentially expressed candidate genes were intersected, and an integrative machine-learning framework-including Boruta, LASSO, XGBoost, and CatBoost-was applied to prioritize shared genes. Integrated machine-learning and network analyses nominated SERPINE1 for further investigation. Single-sample gene set enrichment analysis identified higher scores for porphyrin, folate and pterine, and arachidonic acid metabolism in both disease comparisons. SERPINE1 expression correlated positively with arachidonic acid metabolism scores in both datasets, while Hallmark gene set enrichment analysis linked its expression to inflammatory transcriptional signatures, including TNFA signaling via NFKB and IL6-JAK-STAT3 signaling. Gene interaction, drug-mRNA, transcription factor-mRNA, and competing endogenous RNA networks further characterized its regulatory and pharmacological context. Independent bulk transcriptomic datasets and experimental models supported SERPINE1 upregulation, with single-nucleus RNA-sequencing providing complementary cellular context, while single-nucleus analyses and immunostaining further supported its preferential microglial localization. Collectively, these findings identify SERPINE1 as a shared injury-associated molecular feature of ICH and epilepsy, with preferential microglial localization and associations with inflammatory transcriptional signatures and metabolic pathway scores. Although SERPINE1 is known to be clock-regulated, whether its temporal expression pattern is altered in ICH or epilepsy remains to be determined.

papers.title: In Situ Probing of Small-Molecule Electrolysis Using Ambient-Pressure X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy.
papers.abstract: Electrocatalytic small-molecule conversion addresses the need to couple renewable electricity with sustainable fuel and chemical production, yet challenges remain in resolving the dynamic gas/solid/liquid interfaces that govern catalytic activity, selectivity and stability. A key challenge is to correlate catalyst structures, reaction intermediates and local interfacial environments under comparable operating conditions. Ambient-pressure x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (APXPS) provides surface-sensitive and chemically specific information on catalyst chemical states, interfacial species and local electrostatic environments at the same working interface, enabling direct correlations between catalyst evolution and reaction intermediates. We offer a forward-looking review of APXPS for probing gas/solid/liquid interfaces in small-molecule electrolysis. We discuss three categories of electrochemical XPS/APXPS configurations: quasi-in situ XPS, in which electrochemically treated catalysts are transferred under protected conditions for post-reaction analysis; thin-electrolyte-film (dip-and-pull) APXPS, which probes a potential-controlled interface through a nanometer-scale liquid film; and membrane-based APXPS, which accesses catalyst-ionomer-electrolyte interfaces. We introduce present-day challenges in electrochemical APXPS and describe a vision towards more realistic operating conditions, higher time resolution and multimodal measurements integrated with theoretical and data-driven spectral analysis. These developments provide potential avenues to establish reliable structure-intermediate-environment relationships in the further development of small-molecule electrocatalysis.

papers.title: A Preliminary Examination of Modulation of the LPP by Personal Preference Rankings for Pleasant Experiences.
papers.abstract: The late positive potential (LPP) is a robust neural marker of attention toward emotionally salient stimuli, yet it is unknown how the LPP is modulated by personal preferences for specific types of pleasant objects/experiences. The present study aimed to evaluate whether personal preferences for pleasant experiences modulate the LPP to images reflecting those situations. Secondary analyses examined whether depressive symptoms and a positive emotion intervention were associated with individual differences in this modulation. College students (N = 92; Mage = 19.44, SD = 1.15) reported depressive symptoms before randomization to a positive emotion intervention (n = 47) or study skills comparison group (n = 45). Participants then rank-ordered a list of eight categories of positive objects/experiences (e.g., cute animals, adventure, social activities, junk food) based on which they enjoyed most and viewed images of each while EEG data were recorded. The LPP was modulated by personal preferences broadly, such that the LPP to images depicting top-ranked pleasant categories was enhanced compared to low-ranked pleasant categories; however, significant effects were not observed linearly between each individual ranking. In secondary analyses, depressive symptoms moderated preference effects on the LPP, with greater symptoms associated with less differentiation between highly preferred and less preferred positive stimuli. The positive emotion intervention did not significantly impact LPP modulation by personal preference. Results highlight the utility of considering personal salience in selecting stimuli for clinical neuroscience tasks and indicate that depression may be characterized by difficulty sustaining attention to personally salient pleasant experiences.

papers.title: Amoxicillin-clavulanate-induced neurotoxicity in a patient with end-stage renal disease: a case of reversible encephalopathy.
papers.abstract: Beta-lactam antibiotics are a known but under-recognized cause of neurotoxicity, particularly in patients with renal impairment. While cefepime-associated neurotoxicity is well-described, less attention has been given to amoxicillin-clavulanate. We present a case of a 67-year-old male with end-stage renal disease (ESRD) on chronic intermittent hemodialysis for more than 5 years via a left upper extremity arteriovenous fistula who developed acute encephalopathy characterized by agitation, confusion, and fluctuating consciousness shortly after initiation of 875/125 mg amoxicillin-clavulanate twice daily following hospital discharge. Symptoms began approximately 48 h after antibiotic initiation after the patient had received approximately five total doses, including doses taken before and after a shortened outpatient dialysis session. Symptoms resolved after discontinuation of the medication and completion of inpatient hemodialysis. Extensive workup, including neuroimaging and electroencephalography, was unrevealing. Infectious and metabolic etiologies were excluded based on clinical evaluation and specialist consultation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing antibiotic-induced neurotoxicity in patients with ESRD and emphasizes the risks of inappropriate outpatient dosing at hospital discharge.

papers.title: Association between weekend catch-up sleep and medical expenditure: a longitudinal analysis of the Korean Health Panel Survey.
papers.abstract: Insufficient sleep is increasingly recognized as a major public health concern associated with substantial clinical and economic burden. Although weekend catch-up sleep (WCUS)-the extension of sleep on weekends to compensate for weekday sleep restriction-is a common behavioral response and has been linked to psychological and cardiometabolic benefits, its economic implications remain unknown. This study examined whether WCUS is associated with lower medical expenditure among Korean adults. We analyzed data from 12,634 adults participating in the 2017-2018 Korea Health Panel Survey, a nationally representative longitudinal cohort. WCUS was calculated as the difference between weekend and weekday sleep duration and categorized as non-WCUS (≤ 0 h), short WCUS (≤ 1 h), medium WCUS (≤ 2 h), and long WCUS (> 2 h). The primary outcome was total medical expenditure in 2018, and outpatient, inpatient, and emergency department expenditures were assessed separately. Two-part models-logistic regression for any expenditure and generalized linear models with gamma distribution and log link for positive expenditures-were used to estimate adjusted mean expected expenditures, controlling for sociodemographic, behavioral, clinical, and baseline healthcare utilization variables and accounting for complex survey design. WCUS was strongly and inversely associated with total medical expenditure. Compared with non-WCUS, adjusted marginal reductions were - KRW 589,503 for short WCUS, -KRW 1,278,094 for medium WCUS, and - KRW 1,398,869 for long WCUS, demonstrating a clear dose-response gradient. Outpatient and inpatient expenditures declined steadily with increasing WCUS categories, whereas emergency department expenditures were lowest among individuals with medium WCUS. In analyses stratified by weekday sleep duration, cost reductions were greatest among adults with insufficient weekday sleep (≤ 7 h); medium and long WCUS produced large, statistically significant reductions, whereas short WCUS did not. Among those with sufficient weekday sleep (> 7 h), all WCUS categories were associated with significantly lower expenditures, though with smaller absolute reductions. WCUS was associated with substantially lower annual medical expenditure, with the largest benefits observed among individuals experiencing insufficient weekday sleep. These findings suggest that moderate weekend sleep extension may help offset the economic burden of chronic sleep restriction and represent a practical, low-cost behavioral strategy to reduce health care costs at the population level.

papers.title: Decomposing health inequality by dimensions and determinants in China using EQ-5D-5L: an integrated framework.
papers.abstract: The EQ-5D-5L is a widely used measure of health status that has been increasingly applied to study health inequalities. Despite growing recognition of health as a multidimensional construct, few decomposition studies have simultaneously considered both health dimension and their determinants as sources of inequality. This study fills this gap by providing the first integrated decomposition of socioeconomic-related health inequality in China using the EQ-5D-5L instrument. Using cross-sectional data from a nationally distributed sample of 29,882 Chinese adults, we applied the Erreygers-corrected concentration index (ECI) to measure socioeconomic inequality in EQ-5D-5L utility scores, with household income as the ranking variable. An integrated decomposition framework was developed to jointly quantify the contributions of the five EQ-5D-5L dimensions and their associated determinants to overall health inequality. This framework not only identifies the leading dimensions and determinants but also quantifies how determinants contribute to overall inequality through specific dimensions. The estimated ECI for overall EQ-5D-5L utility scores was 0.0275 (95% confidence interval: 0.0227, 0.0326), indicating modest but statistically significant pro-rich inequality in overall health. Pain/discomfort (PD) and mobility (MO) dimensions jointly accounted for more than 60% of overall inequality. Household income and chronic disease history were primary determinants, which contributed through all five dimensions. Sex-age composition contributed positively to overall inequality but showed an offsetting association with inequality in the anxiety/depression (AD) dimension. Negative life events contributed mainly through the AD and PD dimensions, whereas education was associated with reduced overall inequality via the AD dimension. High malnutrition risk contributed to overall inequality primarily through the MO, usual activities (UA), and SC dimensions, while poor sleep quality contributed predominantly through the AD and PD dimensions. These results were robust to using the Wagstaff-corrected concentration index and an alternative decomposition specification. The contributions of leading determinants to socioeconomic-related health inequality exhibited substantial heterogeneity across health dimensions. Our findings highlight the importance of moving beyond aggregate measures and suggest that interventions informed by the specific determinants and dimensions contributing most to overall inequality may help support more equitable health outcomes in China and other low- and middle-income countries.
papers.journal: International journal for equity in health

papers.title: Machine Learning Improves Questionnaire-Based Sleep Apnea Screening: A Multi-Cohort Multi-Visit Validation Study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) affects a large portion of the global population but remains substantially underdiagnosed due to limited access to polysomnography. While machine learning has shown promise for scalable OSA screening, many recent models rely on overnight physiological monitoring and are not validated across heterogeneous cohorts. This study develops and evaluates questionnaire-based CatBoost models for OSA detection using two large, multi-cohort datasets (SHHS and WSC). The models use 42 easily obtainable features that require no specialized equipment, which could potentially enable highly accessible screening. We assessed performance through comprehensive internal and external validation, including within-cohort external testing (SHHS1 → SHHS2) and cross-cohort generalization (SHHS1 → WSC1), across three clinically relevant AHI cutoffs ( ≥ 5, ≥ 15, ≥ 30 events/h). In internal validation, models achieved consistently balanced performance with AUC 0.74-0.76, sensitivity 67%-73%, and specificity 62%-70% across all cutoffs. Performance remained stable during within-cohort external testing at cutoff ≥ 15 (AUC 0.75, sensitivity 71%, specificity 65%). However, cross-cohort validation revealed noticeable performance degradation due to population distribution shifts, most pronounced at ≥ 5 where specificity dropped substantially (48.5% ± 4.7%) when models trained on the older SHHS cohort were applied to the younger WSC population. SHAP analysis confirmed that predictions relied primarily on established clinical risk factors including neck circumference, age, BMI, and symptom history. These results demonstrate that questionnaire-based machine learning can achieve more balanced sensitivity-specificity trade-offs than traditional scoring rules, and highlight the importance of multi-cohort external testing.

papers.title: Early Responses to Nonconscious Fear-Conditioned Faces-An ERP Study.
papers.abstract: Prioritized processing of emotionally relevant faces compared to neutral faces is reflected in differential event-related potentials (ERPs). However, there is an ongoing debate about the extent to which faces, in general, and fear-conditioned faces, in particular, enhance early ERPs when they are not consciously perceived. Here, we tested whether early ERP components (P1 and N170) differentiate between fear-conditioned (CS+) and non-aversive (CS-) faces presented for 17 ms in a backward-masking design using a sequential Bayesian sampling procedure (N = 40). Consciousness was manipulated by presenting the mask directly (0 ms) or after a delay (200 ms) following the target stimulus. Participants were asked to rate their subjective perception after each trial to differentiate between trials in which they perceived nothing beyond the mask, brief glimpses of anything other than a face, vague impressions of a face, or clear impressions of a face. CS+ as compared to CS- faces led to increased N170 amplitudes in the conscious condition among successfully conditioned participants, but not in the nonconscious condition, while no differential effects were observed for the other ERP components. Thus, the data do not support the assumption that fear-conditioned stimuli are processed nonconsciously in the visual cortex.

papers.title: Mental-Fatigue-Related Changes in EEG Microstate Dynamics and Microstate-Conditioned Phase-Amplitude Coupling.
papers.abstract: Mental fatigue in pilots is a critical risk factor for flight safety. This study aimed to characterize electroencephalographic (EEG) microstate temporal dynamics and microstate-conditioned phase-amplitude coupling across different levels of mental fatigue during a simulated-flight task, and to examine the within-participant associations between these measures. EEG signals were acquired during simulated-flight tasks to analyze neural activity patterns across different mental fatigue levels. The study focused on the temporal parameters of EEG microstates, and the theta-low-beta, theta-high-beta, alpha-low-beta, and alpha-high-beta phase-amplitude couplings (PACs) in the frontal and parietal lobe regions. Linear mixed-effects models were employed to analyze how microstate parameters and PAC metrics varied with mental fatigue levels. Repeated-measures correlations examined within-participant associations between microstate C temporal parameters and PAC under low and high mental fatigue. Compared with the low mental fatigue condition, high mental fatigue was associated with shorter duration, lower occurrence, and lower time coverage of microstate C. Within microstate C, high mental fatigue was associated with higher theta-low-beta PAC in the left parietal and right frontal regions; theta-high-beta PAC in the left frontal, left parietal, and right frontal regions; alpha-low-beta PAC in the bilateral frontal regions; and alpha-high-beta PAC in the right frontal region. Repeated-measures correlations further revealed multiple significant negative within-participant associations between microstate C temporal parameters and microstate C-conditioned PAC under both fatigue conditions. More associations survived FDR correction under high mental fatigue, and most corresponding coefficients were numerically more negative; however, between-condition differences in the correlation coefficients were not formally tested. These findings characterize mental-fatigue-related changes in microstate temporal dynamics and microstate-conditioned PAC, together with exploratory within-participant associations between these measures, and provide new insights into the neural activity patterns associated with mental fatigue.

papers.title: Development of a Simplified Multi-Physics Computational Model of the Coronary Microcirculation.
papers.abstract: Coronary blood flow (CBF) is influenced by multiple biophysical factors, including vascular function (vasoconstriction/vasodilation), structural remodeling (vascular wall thickening), tissue mechanical properties (stiffness), cardiac electrophysiology, and dynamic extravascular forces. However, it is difficult to experimentally determine how these biophysical factors interact to regulate CBF. For example, during type 2 diabetes (T2D) reduced vascular wall stiffness due to reduced coronary vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) stiffness, increased wall thickness due to inward hypertrophic remodeling and increased myocardial stiffness may alter CBF. However, the relative importance of these biophysical factors and their direct effect on CBF is not known. Here, we developed a simplified multi-physics computational model of myocardial tissue deformation and intramyocardial blood flow and used this model to investigate how several biophysical factors influence CBF. This model accounts for excitation-contraction coupling, myocardial fiber structure, dynamic myocardial contraction, passive myocardial mechanical properties, and the mechanics of VSMCs in the coronary microvascular walls. Baseline models yielded CBF velocity waveforms that exhibited peak diastolic velocities and waveform morphologies that were comparable to Doppler echocardiography measurements in normal adult humans. Parameter variation studies were conducted to investigate how several biophysical factors alter the morphological properties of the CBF velocity waveform, and results indicate that VSMC and passive myocardial tissue stiffness were the major drivers of CBF. In addition, the flow regulatory properties of VSMCs were found to depend on the degree of myocardial stiffness. This computational framework represents a new way to investigate how coronary-cardiac interactions regulate CBF.

papers.title: Understanding the patient-experienced trajectory of sleep across the hematopoietic cell transplantation process.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is strongly associated with reduced quality of life and increased anxiety and depression. However, research on what contributes to these negative biobehavioral symptoms among hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) recipients remains limited. This study sought to understand sleep disturbances experienced by allogeneic HCT survivors from the perspectives of patients, clinicians, and caregivers, to identify key contributors to sleep disturbances across the HCT trajectory. This cross-sectional qualitative study included semi-structured interviews with a purposive sample of HCT survivors, caregivers, and clinicians. Interview data were analyzed using an applied thematic approach. Participants (N = 29) were mostly female (69%), White (90%), and non-Hispanic (86%). Clinically relevant time periods emerged in patients' journeys that mark changes in their sleep patterns: during hospitalization, the isolation period after hospitalization, and at home after isolation (i.e., around day +90). In each period, cross-cutting themes emerged that present the trajectory of patients' sleep disturbance throughout the HCT process. Patients continued with poor maladaptive sleep habits acquired during hospitalization after returning home. This study expands research on biobehavioral symptoms among HCT recipients, providing context for quantitative findings in the literature and helping to map the sleep trajectory of allogeneic HCT recipients from multiple perspectives. Future research should consider using the patient, clinician, and caregiver perspectives presented in this work to identify points for targeted interventions that improve patients' sleep and overall quality of life and to advocate for "sleep-friendly" hospital procedures before chronic sleep issues become entrenched.
papers.journal: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

papers.title: Sleep duration: a neglected factor in stroke prevention among individuals with dysglycemia.
papers.abstract: Stroke imposes a staggering and escalating disease burden in China. Individuals with dysglycemia face a markedly elevated risk of incident cerebrovascular events. This study aimed to characterize global and Chinese trends in stroke burden and examine the association between sleep duration and stroke among individuals with dysglycemia, with a particular focus on the potential utility of sleep duration as an behavioral marker for cerebrovascular risk assessment. This study utilized the Global Burden of Disease 2023 database to assess the trends of stroke burden globally and in China(1990-2023). In addition, the study was conducted using data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS), encompassing participants aged ≥ 45 with baseline dysglycemia and no prior stroke. Sleep duration was obtained from the 2020 survey, while incident stroke status was ascertained across the 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020 follow-up waves. Stepwise logistic regression models were employed to evaluate the independent association between baseline sleep duration and new-onset stroke. Restricted cubic splines (RCS) with four knots were applied to explore non-linear dose-response relationships. Additionally, subgroup analyses were conducted to identify effect modifications, and receiver operating characteristic curves evaluated the discriminatory performance of the prediction model including sleep factors. Despite declining global age-standardized rate, the absolute stroke burden in China significantly increased from 1990 to 2023, particularly among males and older adults. In the CHARLS cohort, 7,274 patients with dysglycemia were included in 2011. After a ten-year follow-up, 694 participants (9.54%) developed new strokes. Notably, the sleep duration was significantly longer (9.95 ± 1.74 h hours, P < 0.0001) in the new stroke group. The model after including covariates showed that for every additional hour of sleep, the risk of stroke increased by 22% (OR = 1.22, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.13-1.32). Crucially, RCS analysis uncovered a non-linear inflection point at 7.5-8 h, demonstrating that cerebrovascular risk accelerated rapidly beyond this threshold. The fully adjusted model showed the highest discriminatory performance among the evaluated models, although the overall discrimination remained modest (AUC = 0.666). China's absolute stroke burden continued to surge. Sleep duration may serve as an easily obtainable behavioral marker that complements conventional factors in stroke risk assessment among individuals with dysglycemia.A non-linear association was observed, with stroke risk increasing more rapidly beyond approximately 7.5-8 h of sleep. These findings suggest that sleep duration may provide complementary information for identifying metabolically vulnerable individuals at elevated cerebrovascular risk, although further prospective validation is required. By synergizing human epidemiological expertise with data-driven modeling, this study may provide a feasible approach to complement stroke risk stratification in metabolically vulnerable populations.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: How Is Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Insomnia Provided in Randomized Controlled Trials? A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) in general has demonstrated efficacy in treating insomnia, but there is some variation in the content of CBT for insomnia (CBT-I) across studies. We therefore conducted a scoping review of randomized controlled trials on CBT-I to determine how CBT-I is usually provided in randomized controlled trials. This knowledge is essential for writing evidence-based treatment guidelines and ensuring that clinical practice reflects interventions with proven effectiveness. The search was performed in Pubmed, Embase and Web of Science. A total of 514 publications were included. Excluding the secondary analyses, this left 375 unique randomized controlled trials on CBT-I. A total of 197 focused on comorbid insomnia. The most frequently reported components were stimulus control (86.93%), time-in-bed restriction (84.53%), cognitive therapy (83.20%) and sleep hygiene (78.13%). In a few randomized controlled trials, CBT-I did not include its three core components time-in-bed restriction, stimulus control and cognitive therapy. The reasons for omitting one of these components were rarely reported. The intervention is generally delivered in six sessions, which is more than the previously identified ideal amount of four sessions. When delivered individually, sessions typically lasted 60 min. However, in a group format, they usually lasted 90 min and involved four to six patients. CBT-I was usually delivered in person and by a psychologist. Guidelines on the report of CBT-I in RCTs were formulated.

papers.title: Associations of Frailty, Sleep Quality, and Functional Dependence with Cognitive Function Among Institutionalized Older Adults in Indonesia: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Cognitive impairment is prevalent among older adults in long-term care settings, yet evidence from Indonesian nursing homes remains sparse. To examine cross-sectional associations between frailty, sleep quality, functional dependence, and cognitive function among institutionalized older adults in Indonesia. Methods: A cross-sectional, multi-site study was conducted with 218 residents (aged ≥ 60 years) from three nursing homes in Greater Jakarta (January-March 2026). Cognitive function was measured using the Mini-Mental State Examination, frailty using the FRAIL Scale, sleep quality using the Single-Item Sleep Quality Scale, and functional dependence using the Barthel Index. Hierarchical multiple linear regression was performed adjusting for sociodemographic and clinical covariates. Participants had a mean age of 71.8 years (SD = 7.6); 61.5% were female. Cognitive impairment (MMSE < 24) was identified in 58.7% of participants. In the final model, frailty (β = -.31), sleep quality (β = .24, indicating that better sleep quality was associated with higher cognitive scores), and functional dependence (β = .29) were each independently associated with cognitive performance. The three geriatric syndromes explained 22.6% additional variance, with the overall model accounting for 46.2% of variance (Cohen's f2 = 0.86). Frailty, lower sleep quality, and functional dependence demonstrated independent associations with cognitive impairment in this sample.

papers.title: Overwork and structural alterations in serotonin-melatonin-related brain systems in healthcare workers.
Occupational exposure and neurotoxic health effects in firefighters: toxicological mechanisms and health risks.
papers.abstract: Firefighting involves repeated exposure to combustion products, heat, physical exertion, and sleep disturbances. However, the long-term effects of such exposure on brain health and cognition remain unknown. This narrative review examined the neurotoxic burden associated with firefighting and explored how fireground exposures and stressors may link to neuroinflammation and neurodegenerative diseases. Primary epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro evidence was synthesized; secondary and contextual literature was used for background. A narrative review with a systematic, PRISMA-informed search was performed. PubMed, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Cochrane Library, and EBSCOhost databases were searched for literature published between 1960 and June 2026. The search terms included combinations of firefighter exposure, fire smoke, particulate matter (PM), carbon monoxide (CO), hydrogen cyanide (HCN), polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), neurotoxicity, neuroinflammation, cognitive outcomes, and neurodegenerative diseases. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias assessment was performed. Firefighters are exposed to combustion products via inhalation and dermal contact. CO and HCN can cause hypoxia, leading to ATP depletion and acute neuropsychiatric effects. Fine PM and PAHs may reach the brain, activate glia through NLRP3, and promote ferroptosis and brain aging. Heat stress, fatigue, and sleep disruption may amplify these processes, contributing to cognitive decline and neurodegenerative disorders. Current evidence suggests potential neurological and neurocognitive effects associated with occupational firefighting exposure. However, the available firefighter literature is predominantly cross-sectional, and mechanistic evidence is substantially informed by experimental studies outside firefighter populations. Therefore, causal relationships between occupational exposure and neurodegeneration or brain aging remain uncertain.

papers.title: Innovation and challenges in obstructive sleep apnoea management: a critical review of diagnosis, treatment.
Chrononutrition behaviors and body mass index among university students in the UAE: A cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Emerging evidence suggests that aligning meal timing with the body's circadian rhythms plays a key role in obesity prevention. This study examined the association between chrononutrition-related behaviors, such as preferred and actual eating and sleep timing, duration, latency, and misalignment, and body mass index (BMI) among university students. In this cross-sectional study, sociodemographic data, height, and weight were collected from 302 participants, and chrononutrition indices were assessed using the Chrononutrition Profile Questionnaire (CP-Q). Approximately one-third (32.4%) of participants were having overweight or obesity. Skipping breakfast, long evening latency (time between last meal and bedtime), and discrepancies between preferred and actual sleep durations were significant, albeit weak, predictors of being overweight (p < 0.05). Additionally, misalignments in eating windows and in morning latency (the time between waking and the first meal) predicted obesity and underweight, respectively. Specifically, misalignment in eating windows was associated with obesity, whereas misalignment in morning latency was associated with underweight status. These findings underscore the importance of regularity and timing in both dietary and sleep behaviors and suggest that interventions targeting chrononutrition may support healthy BMI management among university students. Future strategies should consider circadian-aligned meals and sleep patterns to optimize metabolic health in young adults.

papers.title: Prevalence and associated burden of shift work disorder (SWD) in healthcare shift workers in the UK National Health Service (NHS): a cross-sectional survey.
Sex differences in post-traumatic epileptogenesis and neurological dysfunction following traumatic brain injury.
papers.abstract: Post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) is a disabling long-term consequence of traumatic brain injury (TBI), but the role of biological sex on epileptogenesis and recovery remains unclear. Here, we comprehensively characterized chronic PTE development and neurological outcomes in adult male and female mice after severe TBI by controlled cortical impact. Animals underwent continuous video-EEG monitoring for 120 days, serial behavioral, motor, and cognitive testing, and terminal histological assessment of neurodegeneration, neuroinflammation, neurogenesis, and circuit remodeling. Females had a lower incidence of PTE, lower cohort-level seizure burden, a higher seizure threshold, and fewer epileptiform discharges than males. The burden of epileptogenic biomarkers of ripples, fast-ripples, interictal-spikes, and sleep-spindles were also reduced or delayed in females than males. However, among female animals that developed PTE, seizure latency and ictal burden were comparable between sexes, indicating that female sex primarily reduced susceptibility to epilepsy rather than the severity of chronic epilepsy. Females experienced less post-injury health deterioration, recovered neurological and motor function more rapidly, and performed better in recognition-memory and spatial-learning tasks, although chronic cognitive deficits persisted. At 120 days, females showed greater hippocampus neuronal preservation and markedly attenuated astrogliosis and microgliosis than males. Nevertheless, both sexes nevertheless exhibited hippocampal principal neuron and parvalbumin(+) interneuron loss, reduced dentate gyrus neurogenesis, and mossy fiber remodeling. Collectively, these findings identify biological sex as a major determinant of post-traumatic disease trajectory, separating susceptibility to PTE from the severity of epilepsy once established. Sex-stratified outcomes may therefore improve biomarker development and guide sex-specific preventive therapies for PTE. This study reveals a female-resilient phenotype that limits epileptogenesis while leaving chronic network, cognitive deficits, and structural abnormalities unresolved after injury.

papers.title: Repetitive blast TBI drives chronic sex-dependent paroxysmal motor behaviors and sleep disruption.
papers.abstract: Repeated blast-induced traumatic brain injury (rbTBI) is a major cause of chronic neurological morbidity in military populations, with post-traumatic epilepsy (PTE) representing a significant long-term complication. While blast exposure is implicated in epileptogenesis and development of PTE, the direct effects of rbTBI on chronic seizure burden remains poorly understood. This study examined chronic paroxysmal motor behaviors of uncertain origin (PMBs), sleep outcomes, and neuropathology following rbTBI, incorporating sex as a biological variable. Male and female Sprague Dawley rats underwent repeated blast exposure (~20 psi, 24-h intervals) or sham procedures using the McMillan Blast Device. Beginning 4 months post-injury, animals were housed in piezoelectric sleep/seizure monitoring cages for longitudinal assessment of spontaneous PMBs, including myoclonic jerks, wet-dog shakes, and rapid circling/running, and sleep architecture (percent sleep, total sleep, bout length, and sleep-wake transitions) over a 4-week period. At 5 months post-injury, animals were euthanized for immunohistochemical and western blot analysis of astrocytic end-feet expression (AQP4) and glial markers (GFAP, IBA1) in cortex, hippocampus, and corpus callosum. A high proportion of rbTBI animals (80%) developed PMBs, with males showing greater PMB prevalence, frequency, and burden than females. PMBs predominantly occurred during the dark period for both sexes after rbTBI. rbTBI produced chronic sex-specific, transient alterations in sleep architecture, with males showing increased weekly and light-period sleep alongside increased sleep consolidation (longer bout lengths, fewer transitions) from 4 to 5 months post-rbTBI. Females showed a transient reduction in weekly sleep at 4 months post-rbTBI. AQP4 expression was preserved across brain regions regardless of injury or PMB status, indicating chronic recovery of astrocytic end-feet vascular coverage after rbTBI. Hippocampal GFAP was selectively elevated in PMB-positive animals, while whole-brain GFAP protein was significantly increased in rbTBI animals overall, driven primarily by the female rbTBI group, independent of PMB burden. IBA1 expression was unaffected by injury or PMB status. rbTBI produces chronic PMBs and transient disruptions in chronic sleep architecture in male rbTBI animals. Hippocampal astrogliosis is linked to PMB in rbTBI animals and a broader increase in astrogliosis is observed in rbTBI animals, driven by the female rbTBI group. These findings demonstrate persistent sleep and astrocytic alterations alongside chronic paroxysmal motor behaviors after rbTBI, supporting a potential relationship to post-traumatic epileptogenesis.

papers.title: Temporal coupling shapes the effects of prolonged muscle-tendon vibration on sensorimotor EEG activity during motor imagery.
papers.abstract: Motor imagery (MI) recruits sensorimotor networks overlapping those engaged during physical execution and represents a promising rehabilitation tool. While concurrent afferent stimulation enhances MI-related cortical engagement, the effects of prolonged proprioceptive conditioning prior to MI remain unexplored. This study investigated whether prolonged muscle-tendon vibration (MTV) could modulate cortical activity during subsequent MI, indexed by electroencephalographic alpha- and beta-band event-related desynchronization (ERD). Twenty healthy adults performed imagined maximal isometric knee extensions before and after 20-minute suprapatellar MTV (100 Hz) or SHAM vibration (30 Hz with foam interface) in counterbalanced sessions. Cortical engagement was assessed via EEG burst detection over central electrodes (C3, Cz, C4). Maximal force capacity, submaximal force estimation performance, and cortical responses during combined MI and MTV were also evaluated. MTV induced stronger vibratory responses than SHAM, consistent with enhanced proprioceptive afferent activation. Following MTV, voluntary force outcomes showed near-threshold changes consistent with the expected direction, namely reduced maximal force capacity and altered submaximal force calibration, suggesting modified proprioceptive feedback. MI performed after MTV conditioning exhibited reduced alpha- and beta-band ERD compared to SHAM, with greater vibratory-induced responses being associated with a less pronounced post-vibration beta ERD. Conversely, when MI was performed concurrently with MTV following conditioning, alpha-band ERD increased selectively in the MTV session, with no modulation in the beta band. These findings suggest that prolonged proprioceptive conditioning modulates MI-related cortical engagement differently depending on the sensorimotor context in which imagery is performed. Such state-dependent effects may support distinct intervention strategies aimed either at recalibrating maladaptive sensorimotor patterns or at enhancing cortical recruitment in rehabilitation contexts.

papers.title: Repetition Dissociates Pointer and Content-based Representations in Visual Working Memory: Contrasting the CDA with Multivariate Shape Decoding.
papers.abstract: Memorizing a new phone number or address is hard at first, but becomes easier with repetition, as information shifts from working memory to long-term memory. Here we investigated how repetition affects the storage and transition of different aspects of mnemonic information by comparing univariate neural markers of active object storage with multivariate decoding of memory content. Thirty participants encoded lateralized stimuli from a continuous shape space into memory. Memory items were repeated six times in a row to induce learning. In line with earlier work, EEG recordings revealed that repetition led to a reduction in contralateral delay activity (CDA), a measure of active storage that has been taken to reflect a pointer-like representation of the individual object or its original source. In contrast, shape decoding during the retention and also after an impulse perturbation remained constant across repetitions. These results suggest that learning over repetitions reflects the abolishment of active and individuated object memory representations while passive, source-independent memory representations are retained.

papers.title: Age-specific risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone exposure among children aged <18 years.
papers.abstract: Quantifying the risk of fluoroquinolone-associated musculoskeletal and neurological adverse event among children stratified supports clinicians to select the most appropriate antimicrobial regimen for children with bacterial infection. The objective of this study was to assess the risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone exposure, compared with another antimicrobial class using the large-scale database. This retrospective study used the TriNetX platform, a multicenter health record database, to compare risk of musculoskeletal and neurological disorders following fluoroquinolone versus macrolide exposure in children aged <18 years. Propensity score matching was implemented to estimate odds ratio (OR) with 95% confidence interval (CI) of each musculoskeletal and neurological outcome. In the United States, 423,880, 380,504 and 194,220 children aged <5, 5-11 and 12-17 years were matched from each group for the musculoskeletal cohort. The OR of any musculoskeletal outcomes, including disorders of tendon or synovium, in the fluoroquinolone was not increased. Conversely, the OR of peripheral neuropathy and sleep disorder following fluoroquinolone use were 2.22 [1.61-3.06]; p<0.001 and 1.57 [1.44-1.70]; p<0.001, 1.52 [1.20-1.93]; p<0.001 and 1.34 [1.26-1.43]; p<0.001, and 2.18 [1.75-2.72]; p<0.001) and 1.23 [1.13-1.35]; p<0.001 in children aged <5, 5-11, and 12-17 years, respectively. This study showed the increased risk of peripheral neuropathy and sleep disorder following fluoroquinolones use among children compared with macrolide use. This study provided the data for clinicians to estimate risks of musculoskeletal or neurological adverse events.
papers.journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases

papers.title: A reproducible pipeline for simulating individual and inter-brain neural dynamics from structural connectivity.
papers.abstract: Computational models can link anatomical structure to neural dynamics. However, there is no validated, reproducible pipeline that simulates individual and inter-brain EEG-like dynamics from an individual's own structural connectome. To address this, we developed a comprehensive computational pipeline that combines probabilistic tractography from Diffusion Magnetic Resonance Imaging (dMRI) with dynamical systems modeling to simulate EEG-like neural dynamics from individual connectomes. It extracts anatomical connectivity, intra-individual functional connectivity, and inter-individual (two-brain) functional coupling features. It then evaluates their group-discriminative information with random-forest classification under repeated nested cross-validation. Simulated phase-locking values are calibrated against empirical resting-state EEG. In a test sample of individuals with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and matched controls (16 each), simulated intra-individual synchrony added classification information beyond anatomy, raising accuracy from 71.2% (AUC 0.843) to 77.6% (AUC 0.871), in a sample where groups did not differ in mean structural connectivity. Unlike current single-brain simulations, this pipeline generates and jointly simulates two individual brain models within a single system, and reports the contribution of each feature level explicitly. The pipeline provides a reproducible, extensible framework for deriving informative individual-level dynamic features from anatomy. The two-brain extension generates and ranks candidate inter-brain features, providing a principled way to identify between-brain measures for hypothesis-driven testing.

papers.title: Sleep disturbance and enhanced aggression after chronic mild stress in mice: Association with hypothalamic nerve growth factor.
papers.abstract: Chronic stress disrupts sleep and induces behavioural abnormalities. However, the mechanisms linking stress-related sleep disturbances to abnormal social behaviour are unclear. In this study, a predictable chronic mild stress (CMS) paradigm was used, in which male mice were housed on a wire mesh for 3 weeks. CMS mice (n = 7 per group) had reduced non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep and NREM slow-wave activity, and they had enhanced aggressive behaviour, whereas anxiety- and depression-related behavioural measures were not markedly altered. At the molecular level, CMS was associated with lower hypothalamic Ngf mRNA levels, and hypothalamic NGF protein levels were related to aggressive behaviour. Intracerebroventricular administration of NGF promoted sleep in control and CMS mice (n = 6-7 per group), but aggressive behaviour was suppressed only in CMS mice (n = 8 per group). These findings suggest that hypothalamic NGF may contribute to mechanisms that link chronic stress-related sleep disturbances with aggressive behaviour, although the precise downstream mechanisms are not known.

papers.title: Life-long cardiorespiratory consequences of early life stress on estrogen actions in female rats.
papers.abstract: Early-life adversity increases risk for disease with sex-specific effects on brain development. While the association between early-life stress and neuropsychiatric disorders is well established, its impact on respiratory health is poorly documented, particularly in females. Here, we review recent studies using neonatal maternal separation (NMS) to examine the long-term consequences of early-life stress on cardiorespiratory function in females. Panic disorder (PD) is an anxiety disorder that is ⁓2 times more prevalent in women. The respiratory subtype is characterised by an exaggerated ventilatory response to CO2. NMS augmented the response to 5% CO2 of adult female rats; this effect was most pronounced during proestrus and absent in males. Orexin (ORX) neurons potentiate the CO2 response and are normally inhibited by 17β-estradiol (E2). Electrophysiological measurements showed that in control females, excitatory postsynaptic current frequency varied inversely with E2 levels. However, NMS disrupted this E2-mediated inhibition, particularly during proestrus, implicating impaired estrogen action in PD-related respiratory dysfunction. Age-related ovarian decline increases the risk of sleep apnea and associated comorbidities. Whereas apnea frequency decreased with age in control females, 1 year-old NMS females exhibited a 75% higher apnea index than age-matched controls, together with greater adiposity and hypertension. Arterial pressure was inversely correlated with circulating E2 levels only in NMS females, indicating heightened vulnerability to age-related estrogen decline. Although physiological fluctuations in E2 levels exert modest effects in healthy females, we propose that early-life stress persistently alters responsiveness to E2 and acts synergistically with ageing to increase cardiovascular vulnerability throughout the female lifespan.

papers.title: Treatment of a concealed accessory pathway by radiofrequency catheter ablation in a horse.
papers.abstract: Accessory pathways (APs) are myocardial bundles directly connecting the atria and the ventricles, bypassing the atrioventricular node-His-Purkinje system. Retrograde AP conduction in horses can result in orthodromic atrioventricular re-entry tachycardia or bradycardia. Radiofrequency catheter ablation (RFCA) can provide a permanent treatment by eliminating the retrograde conducting AP, but was previously unsuccessful in one case. To report the use of three-dimensional electro-anatomical mapping (3D EAM) to identify a concealed AP and treatment by RFCA in a horse. Retrospective case report. An irregular heart rhythm was detected in a 4-year-old, 518 kg Paint mare as an incidental finding. Frequent atrial depolarisations were identified in the ST segment with a fixed coupling interval to the preceding QRS complex on the ECG. A differential diagnosis of frequent premature atrial complexes displayed as bigeminy or a retrograde conduction along an AP was made. The presence of a retrograde conducting AP was confirmed by ventricular pacing, which resulted in 1:1 ventriculo-atrial activation. Three-dimensional EAM revealed the earliest atrial activation and thereby the atrial insertion of the AP in the caudal left atrium. Subsequent RFCA at 40 W eliminated AP conduction. Single case report. This case report describes the identification of an AP by 3D EAM and the first successful permanent treatment of a retrograde conducting AP by RFCA in an adult horse.

papers.title: Respiratory control instability during sleep is associated with incident atrial fibrillation.
papers.abstract: There is an association between central sleep apnea (CSA) and atrial fibrillation (AF). However, standard scoring and threshold criteria for CSA are relatively rigid and does not capture the entirety of expressed high loop gain (HLG) of the respiratory control system during sleep. We aimed to investigate the association between HLG sleep apnea, as measured by a respiratory self-similarity (SS) detection algorithm, and the risk of incident AF. Polysomnograms from the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) and the Osteoporotic Fractures in Men Study (MrOS) were analyzed to quantify expressed HLG using an automated algorithm that calculates SS% and a Central Respiratory Event Index (CREI). Multivariable Logistic regression models were used to assess the relationship between HLG metrics and incident AF. A total of 3706 participants (2897 from SHHS and 809 from MrOS) were included. In MrOS, high SS% (≥13.5%) and high CREI (≥30 events/hour) remained significantly associated with incident AF after mutual adjustment with CSA (SS%: OR 1.697, 95% CI 1.027-2.805, p: 0.039; CREI: OR 1.661, 95% CI 1.022-2.699, p: 0.041). In SHHS participants <65 years, SS% >10.5% was associated with AF after full adjustment (OR 3.613, 95% CI 1.347-9.693, p: 0.011) and remained significant after adjustment for CSA (OR 7.661, 95% CI 1.875-31.309, p: 0.005). Expressed high loop gain sleep apnea is independently associated with incident atrial fibrillation in community-based cohorts.

papers.title: AI-enabled Vectorcardiography (AI-VCG) combined with cardiac magnetic resonance for the mechanism of left bundle branch block in patients undergoing cardiac resynchronization therapy.
papers.abstract: Left bundle branch block (LBBB) is a heterogeneous conduction disorder with major implications for cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT). Conventional ECG criteria incompletely distinguish intact Purkinje activation (IPA-LBBB) from complete conduction block (CCB-LBBB), limiting precision pacing decisions. To develop an AI-based, patient-specific vectorcardiographic (AI-VCG) framework that integrates ECG and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) to noninvasively identify LBBB mechanisms. A patient-specific AI-VCG model was constructed using individualized ECG-to-VCG transformations derived from cardiac-torso geometry and expressed in cardiac-centric coordinates. Performance was evaluated using in-silico electrophysiology simulations (n = 48 hearts) and a clinical CRT cohort (n = 38). A physiologically interpretable AI-VCG feature-the integral of the left-right cardiac vector (IcX)-was assessed for mechanism classification. In-silico validation demonstrated strong discrimination of IPA-LBBB versus CCB-LBBB (AUROC 0.96). The clinical IcX analysis separated IPA-LBBB and CCB-LBBB with 100% accuracy in the LBBB subset (n = 25), with a 22.4 μWb gap between the highest IPA and lowest CCB IcX values. Direct comparator analyses showed 100% accuracy for Kors-derived QRS area (but with a narrower gap), 76% accuracy for Strauss criteria, and 68% accuracy for sex-specific QRS duration alone. A patient-specific AI-VCG framework provides an explainable, noninvasive and anatomically grounded representation of LBBB mechanisms. These preliminary results support further validation against conventional ECG and VCG metrics in larger multicenter cohorts.

papers.title: Multilevel predictors of sleep quality trajectories in patients with heart failure: an application of the social-ecological model of sleep health.
papers.abstract: Poor sleep quality is common in patients with heart failure, yet its heterogeneous trajectories and multilevel predictors remain unclear. To identify heterogeneous trajectories of sleep quality and explore their multilevel predictors among patients with heart failure during the hospital-to-home transition. We recruited 227 patients with heart failure from the cardiology departments of three tertiary hospitals in China using a longitudinal study design. Sleep quality was assessed pre-discharge and at 1, 3, and 6 months post-discharge. Baseline predictors across individual, interpersonal and societal levels were assessed before patient discharge, including sociodemographic and clinical characteristics, physical symptoms, sleep beliefs and attitudes, mutuality, nighttime light, and pre-sleep electronic screen exposure. Latent growth mixture modeling was employed to identify sleep quality trajectories, and multinomial logistic regression was used to explore predictors of trajectory membership. Three trajectories were identified: poor-persisted (18.5%), poor-alleviated (6.6%) and good-persisted (74.9%). Patients with severe physical symptoms, nighttime light exposure, and pre-sleep electronic screen exposure (≥ 2 h) tended to be in the "poor-persisted" group, whereas those with positive sleep beliefs and attitudes were more likely to be in the "good-persisted" group. Nearly one-fifth of patients with heart failure experience persistently poor sleep quality during 6 months after discharge. These findings support early screening and follow-up assessment of patients at risk of persistent poor sleep quality. Relieving physical symptoms, modifying negative sleep beliefs and attitudes, and reducing nighttime light and electronic screen exposure may be potential targets for multilevel sleep management in patients with heart failure.
papers.journal: Heart & lung : the journal of critical care

papers.title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances exposure is associated with sleep problems in children: Multi-omics evidence.
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants that may pose health risks to children. Sleep is essential for children's physical, cognitive, and behavioral development, yet the environmental determinants of sleep problems remain poorly understood. Despite widespread PFAS exposure, evidence regarding their association with sleep disorders and the underlying mechanisms remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between PFAS mixture exposure and sleep disorders in children and to identify PFAS-associated molecular signatures and potential biological pathways through integrated proteomic and lipidomic analyses. A total of 135 children were included, and a quartile-based scoring approach was used to construct a PFAS mixture index. Multivariable linear regression was performed to evaluate associations between PFAS exposure and sleep disorders, with the total score of the Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire (CSHQ) as the primary outcome. Serum PFAS concentrations were measured using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and proteomic and lipidomic profiling were conducted using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry. Higher PFAS exposure was associated with increased CSHQ scores (β = 0.243, 95%CI: 0.012, 0.474, P = 0.040). Multi-omics analysis identified 270 PFAS-associated proteins and 139 PFAS-associated lipids (P < 0.05). The Antigen processing and presentation pathways emerged as a potential mediator, while sphingolipid metabolism was significantly enriched among the PFAS-associated lipids. These findings suggest that PFAS exposure is associated with sleep disorders in children and may be linked to alterations in immune-related pathways and lipid metabolism, offering preliminary insights into the potential biological pathways underlying this association.

papers.title: Educational level stratifies clinical profiles and oxygen desaturation index-associated factors in middle-aged and elderly Chinese patients with sleep-disordered breathing.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to explore differences in demographic, clinical, and psychological characteristics among middle-aged and elderly Chinese patients with moderate-to-severe sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) across educational levels, and to identify factors associated with the oxygen desaturation index (ODI) as well as potential statistical indirect effects. We further examined whether educational level moderates the relationship between psychological symptoms and ODI. A total of 306 patients with moderate-to-severe SDB were recruited with strict exclusion criteria. All participants underwent overnight monitoring with a wrist pulse oximeter to calculate ODI (oxygen desaturation events ≥3% lasting ≥3 s per hour). Demographic information, medical history, and questionnaire scores (sleepiness, insomnia, anxiety, depression, fatigue, quality of life) were collected. Patients were divided into lower (primary school or unschooled) and higher (junior high school or above) educational level groups. A predefined multivariable linear regression model and statistical mediation analysis were used. Age- and sex-adjusted group comparisons were performed. Among 306 patients, 178 were in the lower educational level group and 128 in the higher educational level group. After age and sex adjustment, the higher educational level group had higher ODI, BMI, monthly income, alcohol use, daytime sleepiness, insomnia, anxiety, and depression scores, but less fatigue. Educational level was not independently associated with ODI after multivariable adjustment. In the overall sample, BMI (standardized beta = 0.252, P < 0.001) and average monthly income (standardized beta = 0.24, P = 0.001) were independent correlates of ODI. BMI statistically accounted for 27.3% of the association between average monthly income and ODI. Subgroup analyses using the predefined regression model showed that GAD-7 anxiety score was positively associated with ODI in the lower educational level group (standardized beta = 0.372, P < 0.05), while BMI (standardized beta = 0.324, P = 0.002) and average monthly income (standardized beta = 0.219, P = 0.048) were positively associated with ODI in the higher educational level group. The higher education subgroup findings were consistent with the overall sample results. Educational level is not directly associated with ODI but stratifies distinct clinical and psychological profiles and heterogeneous ODI-associated factors in patients with SDB. In the lower education group, anxiety (GAD-7) emerges as an independent correlate of ODI, while in the higher education group, BMI and income predominate, findings consistent with the overall sample. BMI and income are independent correlates with ODI, with BMI statistically accounting for a portion of the income-ODI association. These cross-sectional findings highlight the need for education-stratified approaches to SDB assessment, with particular attention to anxiety symptoms in lower-educated populations.

papers.title: Cortical-fluidic dimensional mapping isolates GRIN2A-driven dysconnectivity and pharmacological network degradation in schizophrenia.
papers.abstract: Standard connectivity models fail to capture the transient spatial kinematics underlying schizophrenia pathophysiology. The present study introduces Cortical-Fluidic Dimensional Mapping to resolve this analytical limitation. The framework translates continuous high-density electroencephalography into a dynamic fluid system to quantify instantaneous spatial turbulence. The algorithm processed over 7000 memory testing sessions from 364 healthy participants. The validation phase evaluated a pre-existing clinical repository comprising 300 de-identified psychiatric records. The investigation isolated functional dysconnectivity driven by the GRIN2A genetic variant and specific neurochemical modulations. The C-C genotype triggers a profound inversion of functional connectivity in the cuneus to caudate pathway, indicating a critical collapse in sensory gating mechanisms. Midazolam suppresses network turbulence heavily. Ketamine induces widespread hyperconnectivity across the networks. Lamotrigine mitigates this aberrant ketamine-driven state successfully. The physiological parameters directly mirror the cognitive deficits. Cuneus dysconnectivity links strictly to global symptom severity. The methodology establishes an objective biomarker. The framework maps the exact spatial consequences of N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor hypofunction. The metrics quantify the dysconnection hypothesis directly. The system links molecular glutamatergic vulnerabilities to macroscopic neural degradation in treatment-resistant psychiatric conditions.

papers.title: Theoretical and Experimental Study of Photoacoustic Spectral Intraoperative Pathological Assessment Using Oral and Breast Cases.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative, label-free pathological assessment of surgical margins remains a long-standing challenge. Here, we propose an intraoperative pathological diagnostic method based on broadband Photoacoustic Spectral Analysis (bPASA) and validate it from theoretical and experimental perspectives. Theoretically, we employed a spherical droplet framework to study how variations in nuclear radius, acoustic velocity, and density affect photoacoustic spectral features. Experimentally, we used Polystyrene (PS) and Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA) microspheres of varying sizes as nuclear phantoms, yielding strong agreement with theoretical predictions and enabling clear discrimination between phantom types. Further, we performed pathological assessment on mouse breast and oral tissues under three specimen forms: tissue sections, fresh tissues, and in vivo samples, and demonstrated that bPASA consistently discriminated between normal and cancerous tissues across all forms. Together, these findings establish bPASA as a rapid, label-free method for intraoperative pathological assessment, offering crucial support for the intraoperative identification of malignant tumors.

papers.title: Digital rehabilitation interventions for Fibromyalgia: A scoping review.
papers.abstract: Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterised by widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and cognitive-emotional symptoms. Digital health interventions may help improve access to care and support self-management. To map the characteristics, delivery formats, outcomes, and assessment instruments of digital health interventions for adults with fibromyalgia. The review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched in February 2026. Eligible studies evaluated digital interventions in adults (≥18 years) with fibromyalgia. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. A descriptive synthesis was conducted to map intervention characteristics, delivery modes, outcome domains, and assessment instruments. Twenty-nine studies published between 2010 and 2025 were included. Four intervention categories were identified: emotional or behavioural programmes, exercise-based telerehabilitation, self-management or educational interventions, and multicomponent programmes. Interventions were delivered asynchronously (n = 16), synchronously (n = 8), or using hybrid formats (n = 3). The most frequently assessed outcomes were pain, fibromyalgia impact, fatigue, sleep, psychological variables, and physical functioning. Overall, digital interventions were associated with favourable physical and psychosocial outcomes. More consistent benefits were reported for supervised interventions, particularly exercise-based telerehabilitation and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy or Cognitive Behavioural Therapy-based programmes, whereas unguided app-based interventions showed more variable findings. Digital interventions appear to be a promising approach for supporting rehabilitation and symptom management in fibromyalgia. However, substantial heterogeneity in intervention characteristics, delivery modes, outcome measures, and study designs remains. Greater standardisation, longer follow-up periods, and more rigorous studies are needed.

papers.title: Sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations, 2000-2025: a layered bibliometric and science-mapping analysis.
papers.abstract: We characterised the growth, composition and intellectual structure of sleep and circadian research across critical care settings and populations from 2000 to 2025, with particular attention to the representation and citation visibility of Nursing-category journals. Web of Science Core Collection Article and Review records retrieved on 1 August 2026 yielded 4760 after deduplication. A deterministic title/author-keyword rule gave a field-central corpus of 1047 nested in an abstract-inclusive corpus of 3588. Two authors independently assessed a 200-record stratified sample. Growth, annual Nursing-category share and citations were modelled using log-linear, binomial logistic and negative binomial regression, respectively. Reporting followed the preliminary guideline for reporting bibliometric reviews of the biomedical literature (BIBLIO). The corpus held 859 Articles and 188 Reviews from 370 sources (29,660 citations; h-index 79), growing 15.30%/year (95% confidence interval [CI] 13.73-16.89). Nursing-category journals produced 21.2% of 2000-2024 records, with increasing annual odds (odds ratio [OR] 1.041, 95% CI 1.009-1.075; p = 0.013), but accounted for 13.3% of citations and 1 of the 46 most-cited records (2.2%). Median analysis did not detect a difference. Coupling of 84 highly cited documents yielded five multi-publication clusters with mean years from 2006.6 to 2016.6. Layer choice materially changed influential-publication rankings. Human validation yielded a positive predictive value (PPV) of 92.0% (95% CI 84.8-96.5%). The field expanded substantially. Among highly cited publications, older clusters concerned sleep physiology and later clusters included interventions and guidance. Nursing-category journals were under-represented in the upper citation tail. The map can help critical care teams locate literature on sleep assessment, environmental modification and care clustering across patient, survivor and staff populations. Searches for sleep-related guidance should include Nursing-category and multidisciplinary critical-care journals.

papers.title: Comprehensive benchmarking of EEG biomarkers for Parkinson's disease: robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability across multiple datasets.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) provides a high-temporal-resolution, noninvasive window into some of the abnormalities underlying Parkinson's disease (PD), yet reported electrophysiological biomarkers vary widely across studies due to differences in preprocessing, feature extraction, and analytical pipelines. Here we provide the first comprehensive, multi-dataset benchmarking of 16 EEG-derived biomarkers, including phase-amplitude coupling, beta burst metrics, aperiodic components, complexity measures, and beta waveform features, to evaluate their robustness, reliability, and clinical discriminability. Using three independent resting-state EEG datasets, with two preprocessing conditions evaluated for one dataset, we assessed the effects of preprocessing, window length, within-session variability, channel aggregation strategies, and clinical group differences (healthy controls vs. PD OFF-medication, healthy controls vs. PD ON-medication, and PD OFF- vs. ON-medication). Cross-dataset reproducibility of group-level effects was additionally evaluated using effect-size pattern similarity, biomarker rank concordance, effect-direction consistency, and random-effects meta-analysis. Aperiodic features, entropy and complexity measures, and fractal metrics demonstrated high methodological robustness across preprocessing methods, window lengths, and aggregation strategies, and several showed disease- and medication-related effects across datasets, although effect magnitude and statistical significance varied across datasets and analytical conditions. In contrast, oscillatory biomarkers, including beta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling, burst-derived metrics, and waveform-asymmetry features, showed substantial variability across methodological choices and lower within-session consistency. However, this methodological sensitivity should not necessarily be interpreted as lower biological relevance, as these measures may capture more transient or state-dependent physiological dynamics. Fully-denoised data improved group-level separability, for several biomarkers in Dataset 1. Together, these findings identify several biomarkers with comparatively strong methodological robustness for further biological and clinical validation and highlight methodological factors that contribute to inconsistencies in the PD literature. This benchmarking framework provides practical guidance for standardizing biomarker analysis while emphasizing that methodological robustness, biological sensitivity, and clinical utility represent distinct dimensions of biomarker performance.

papers.title: Coverage collapse and deceptive calibration in EEG fatigue monitoring: a cross-dataset audit under within-session and cross-subject shift.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography-based driver fatigue monitors are judged almost entirely on accuracy, yet a safety monitor is useful only if its stated confidence can be trusted when it is wrong. We audit whether it survives drift within a recording and transfer to a new person.Approach. Five model families, from a dense network to a gradient-boosted tree ensemble, run on three public corpora differing in channels, label instrument and elicitation. Calibration is measured pooled, per recording and per class, beside proper scoring rules. Seven conformal recalibration strategies are compared under one protocol, and we derive a ceiling on the coverage attainable by any rule thresholding a fixed calibration set.Main results. Pooled calibration error falls as accuracy falls, so the headline reliability metric improves as the model degrades. Aggregated per recording, the same predictions reverse it, exceeding the pooled estimate in all fifteen session-time bins of both continuously annotated corpora (sign test, p = 3.1 × 10⁻⁵); on the fatigued class the concealed error reaches 4.9 times the pooled value. Under transfer, class-balanced calibration error rises by 0.107 to 0.254 in all fifteen model-corpus cells, where coverage falls below its 0.90 target, to 0.533 at worst, with empty prediction sets in four. The ceiling held on all 32 subject streams and bound 20 below target, separating recoverable methods in advance. Rolling re-estimation under a finite-sample correction cleared it on 19 of those 20, held 0.886 to 0.909 in every cell, and cut between-subject coverage variability from 0.205 to 0.026 at constant update cost.Significance.
