Pooled calibration error and marginal coverage can both look healthy while a monitor is least reliable in the states that should raise an alarm. Three cheap diagnostics separate a calibrated monitor from one averaging failures of opposite sign, and one that covers from one that abstains.

papers.title: Beyond screen time: Evidence-based assessment and early intervention for problematic digital use in young people.
papers.abstract: Screen-based technologies are now embedded in the daily routines of children and adolescents and offer important developmental, educational and social benefits. However, excessive use can contribute to sleep disruption, emotional distress, behavioural difficulties and family conflict. General practitioners (GPs) are often the first point of contact for families concerned about their child's digital behaviours, yet many GPs report uncertainty about how best to assess risk, provide practical advice and identify when specialist input is required. This paper provides evidence-informed guidance for GPs on assessing problematic screen use, supporting families with prevention and early intervention strategies, and recognising when referral to mental health or paediatric services is indicated. Clinical assessment should prioritise functional impairment and associated psychosocial impacts rather than focusing solely on screen-time duration. GPs can draw on validated indicators of problematic use, implement family-based prevention strategies and screen for co-occurring mental health conditions. Referral to specialist services is indicated when significant impairment persists or when safety concerns arise.

papers.title: Advantages and Limitations of Minipigs in Cardiovascular Safety Pharmacology and Toxicology Studies in Drug Development.
papers.abstract: Minipigs are recognized as a relevant non-rodent species for nonclinical safety assessment in drug development, although their use remains considerably less common than that of dogs and non-human primates. Historically cited barriers to broader adoption have included increased test article requirements due to their larger size, limited historical control data, technical challenges, and limited experience with their use in nonclinical safety assessment. However, some of these limitations have been mitigated in recent years. While minipigs are most often used for dermally administered drugs due to similarities in skin structure, they are also considered a highly relevant model for cardiovascular research due to similarities in anatomy and physiology with the human cardiovascular system. In this review, we evaluate the advantages and limitations of using minipigs in nonclinical safety assessment for predicting human cardiovascular effects. We summarize current knowledge of porcine cardiovascular anatomy, electrophysiology, hemodynamics, and pharmacokinetics, and discuss how these parameters influence the translational relevance of the minipig model.

papers.title: Distinct Splicing Complexes Formed by RS2Z32 Isoforms Modulate Alternative Splicing and Flowering.
papers.abstract: Serine/arginine (SR) splicing factors can alter downstream precursor messenger RNA (pre-mRNA) splicing patterns and influence gene expression. However, the influences of different isoforms generated by alternative splicing of SR proteins themselves on the transcription and splicing of downstream target genes in plants remain to be elucidated. Here, we demonstrate that the interaction between arginine/serine-rich zinc knuckle-containing protein 32 (RS2Z32) splicing isoforms and the Arabidopsis thaliana ortholog of human splicing factor SC35 (SC35) leads to the formation of distinct complexes, through which the recognition of splice sites within intron 3 of the transcription factor circadian clock associated 1 (CCA1) gene is regulated, ultimately resulting in an altered ratio of the CCA1 splice variants. Competitive binding of CCA1α and CCA1β to the flowering locus C (FLC) gene promoter can either promote or inhibit FLC transcription and flowering. This study elucidates the molecular mechanism by which RS2Z32 regulates FLC expression independently of its canonical splicing function, enhancing our understanding of transcriptional regulation mediated by splicing factors in plants.

papers.title: Experience and Perception of Sleep Symptoms Among Black Survivors of Localized Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: To explore and describe sleep quality, sleep duration, and sleep disturbances among Black survivors of non-small cell lung cancer (stages I-IIIa). 15 Black survivors completed an in-person interview after completing a weeklong in-home sleep assessment. Participants were primarily recruited via cancer registry data from a medical and radiation oncology practice in the southeastern United States. This qualitative, descriptive study was guided by the University of California, San Francisco, symptom management theory. Interviews were conducted, audio recorded, transcribed, and coded and categorized using reflexive thematic analysis. The following five themes emerged: (a) Perceived sleep quality varied from terrible to good; (b) multiple wakes occurred after sleep onset; (c) upon final awakening, survivors did not feel well rested; (d) a sleep-time routine is perceived as beneficial to improve sleep quality; and (e) health providers are inattentive to sleep being a consistent clinical problem. This study provides new evidence that sleep is an important clinical problem among Black survivors of localized non-small cell lung cancer, a historically understudied population. This study supports more effective assessment and intervention strategies to understand and improve sleep.

papers.title: A practical machine learning approach to identifying adverse effects due to COVID-19 vaccines.
papers.abstract: This study aims to elucidate potential connections between various health-related factors and reported adverse effects (AEs) following COVID-19 vaccination. Using the "snowball sampling" method, we collected data from 301 Brazilians participants, both sexes, who underwent COVID-19 vaccination during SARS-CoV-2 pandemic. We also collected data from general health status, vaccine type received, sleep quality, physical activity levels, dietary habits, alcohol consumption, history of COVID-19 infection, and the use of chronic medications. Employing a decision tree regression (DTR) model, we sought to unravel intricate associations between lifestyle, health profile, and AEs attributed to COVID-19 vaccines. Our DTR analysis revealed that AEs tended to be lower in older individuals, with sleep quality further influencing this decrease (all P≤0.02). Intriguingly, individuals with suboptimal sleep efficiency were also users of medication, and notably, medication usage appeared to mitigate AEs in this subgroup (all P≤0.01). Here, we demonstrate that the DTR is a valuable model for investigating the AEs related to COVID-19 vaccines. In summary, our findings underscore the impact of age, sleep efficiency, and medication use for non-COVID-19-related conditions in explaining the observed AEs following COVID-19 vaccination.

papers.title: [Unveiling remote study conditions during the COVID-19 pandemic and the associations with food insecurity].
papers.abstract: The objective was to identify the profile of emergency remote study (ERS) conditions, food (in)security and existing associations, in a population of 2,361 students from Brazilian Universities, in the first wave of COVID-19. Based on Mercuri (1992), material (technological, connectivity, furniture), temporal (course period), spatial (home) and personal (hours of sleep) factors were used to identify the construct remote study (RS) conditions using latent class analysis. Pearson chi-square and multinomial regression tested the associations. A population was found to be mostly female, unmarried, with income <R$ 3,000.00. Food insecurity was identified in 44.4% of households. The model with 4 classes characterized the ERS conditions as Vulnerable (LC1), Adequate (LC2), Risk (LC3) and Imbalanced (LC4), with a higher proportion in LC1 (32,2%). Moderate/severe food insecurity was associated with LC1 and LC3, demonstrating that students lived simultaneously with hunger and inadequate conditions to study during the pandemic. Mitigating the effects of COVID-19, especially among the most affected groups, is the role of public policies, inside and outside universities.

papers.title: Prognostic Implications of High HFpEF Probability in Patients With Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension.
papers.abstract: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and left heart disease, particularly heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), show overlapping clinical features despite distinct pathophysiology. The HFpEF-ABA algorithm (age, body mass index, atrial fibrillation) was used to characterize HFpEF pretest probability in patients with CTEPH and evaluate its association with left heart disease and clinical worsening. Among 466 patients with CTEPH stratified by HFpEF-ABA score (low < 25%, intermediate 25%-74%, high ≥ 75%), Spearman's correlation assessed associations with common left heart disease comorbidities. Kaplan-Meier analysis and Cox regression evaluated associations with clinical worsening, with restricted cubic splines assessing the dose-response relationship and non-linearity. Subgroup analyses by sex, smoking, alcohol use, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and obstructive sleep apnea assessed the consistency. We also evaluated whether adding the HFpEF-ABA score improved COMPERA 2.0 discrimination for clinical worsening. Intermediate and high HFpEF probability was found in 52.4% (n = 244) and 9.0% (n = 42), respectively. After adjustment, each standard deviation increase in HFpEF probability was associated with an approximately 73% increase in clinical worsening (p < 0.001). Results were consistent for HFpEF probability (p < 0.05), with no significant subgroup interactions. Adding HFpEF-ABA with COMPERA 2.0 improved discrimination, increasing the C-index increasing from 0.532 to 0.634 (p = 0.012). Assessing HFpEF probability in patients with CTEPH identifies those at high risk for this comorbidity and improves the precision when integrated with existing risk models.
keywords: heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

papers.title: Polysomnography harmonization schemes: A multi-institutional sleep research resource.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are associated with cardiovascular diseases and cognitive decline worldwide, highlighting the need for effective therapeutic strategies. Polysomnography (PSG) is the gold standard diagnostic tool for sleep disorders. However, long examination times, high costs, specialized biosignal equipment and controlled settings requirements hinder large-scale data collection. As artificial intelligence applications in sleep research expand, structural heterogeneity in PSG data across institutions complicates multi-center integration, increases preprocessing burden, and limits reproducible large-scale algorithm validation. We investigated biosignals, sleep parameters, and demographic features from eight publicly available PSG datasets. A set of schemas for PSG harmonization is proposed to formalize unified structural specifications aligned with established clinical guidelines. These schemas systematically integrate heterogeneous biosignals, derived sleep parameters, and demographic features to achieve consistent attribute selection and uniform preprocessing across datasets. When applied to construct an integrated dataset, the schemas demonstrated stable demographic and clinical distributions through repeated sampling. By addressing schema-level interoperability, the proposed framework facilitates consistent algorithm evaluation and comparison and provides a structured reference for reproducible, large-scale sleep research.

papers.title: The effects of angel sounds and guided imagery technique played to expectant couples on attachment, anxiety and sleep quality.
papers.abstract: The authors aimed to investigate the effects of listening to fetal heart sounds (FHS), metaphorically referred to as "angel sounds," and guided imagery technique (GIT) on prenatal attachment, anxiety, and sleep quality among expectant couples. A randomized controlled trial was conducted with nFHS = 59couples, nGIT = 59couples, and nControl = 59couples. Experimental group participants received nightly pre-sleep interventions for three consecutive nights. Fetal heart sounds were played for at least 20 min in the FHS group, and imaginary recordings containing different scenarios were played daily in the GIT group. Data were collected using Personal Information Forms, Maternal and Paternal Antenatal Attachment Scales, State Anxiety Inventory,and Richard-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire. FHS was more effective than GIT in reducing anxiety in women. FHS and GIT are effective non-pharmacological interventions for enhancing attachment and sleep quality in expectant couples (p < 0.05). These interventions may be integrated into routine prenatal care and offer a couple-centered approach to psychosocial support during pregnancy.

papers.title: Social jetlag and DXA-derived adiposity in Korean adults: A nationwide study using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey.
papers.abstract: Social jetlag, the discrepancy between weekday and weekend sleep timing, is a behavioral marker of circadian timing mismatch and has been linked to obesity, mainly through conventional anthropometric measures. We examined its association with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived adiposity using the nationally representative 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥40 years reporting usual weekday and weekend bedtimes and wake times. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as <1 h, 1- < 2 h, and ≥2 h, with ≥2 h as the primary exposure. The primary outcome was DXA-derived total body fat percentage; subtotal and trunk fat percentages were key secondary outcomes. Height, weight, and waist circumference were obtained by standardized KNHANES examination. Survey-weighted linear regression was adjusted for age, sex, height, average sleep duration, income, education, smoking, alcohol use, physical activity, hypertension, and diabetes. Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h. In fully adjusted models, this group had higher total body fat percentage (β = 0.81 percentage points; P = 0.025), subtotal fat percentage (β = 0.86; P = 0.025), and trunk fat percentage (β = 1.01; P = 0.036), but not higher BMI or waist circumference. Associations persisted after adjustment for depressive symptoms, but were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment for a chronotype-related proxy, and were not reproduced when social jetlag was corrected for sleep debt. Sleep duration variability showed no association. Social jetlag ≥2 h was associated with modestly higher DXA-derived total and trunk body fat percentage, differences not captured by BMI or waist circumference. Because the associations did not persist in chronotype-adjusted or sleep-corrected analyses, conventional social jetlag may partly reflect compensatory weekend sleep. These findings are hypothesis-generating and need longitudinal confirmation.

papers.title: Evaluation of family functioning, parental awareness, life satisfaction, stress levels, and clinical findings in children with sleep bruxism.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the relationship between sleep bruxism and family functioning, parental awareness, life satisfaction, and stress levels, as well as to examine clinical findings. Eighty-two children aged 8-11 years with sleep bruxism and their parents were included. Intraoral and extraoral examinations were performed. Parental awaneress, family functioning, life satisfaction, and stress levels were assesed by questions or scales. Chi-square tests, Pearson correlation analysis, independent-samples t-tests, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA), and post-hoc tests were used. More than half of the parents (51.2%) reported having knowledge about sleep bruxism, and 35.4% identified psychological factors as its cause. Muscle and temporomandibular joint tenderness on palpation was observed in 13.4% of the children, while 7.3% reported morning jaw muscle pain or fatigue. A total of 54.9% of the parents demonstrated poor family functioning. Children showed high perceived stress, while parents exhibited low-to-moderate stress and moderate life satisfaction. Positive correlations were observed between dental caries and wear and family functioning (p < .05). Children with sleep bruxism were accompanied by elevated stress levels, poor family functioning, and low parental awareness. These findings underscore the importance of integrating psychosocial and clinical approaches in pediatric sleep bruxism management.
papers.journal: Cranio : the journal of craniomandibular practice

papers.title: Mirror Neural System in Hands Motor Imagery with Pictures and Videos Guidance: An EEG-fNIRS Study.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) achieved by motor imagery (MI) have been widely accepted as an effective tool in rehabilitative applications. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) and electroencephalography (EEG) are two common implementation forms of BCIs, capable of monitoring neuronal potential changes and hemodynamic variations during different tasks. MI and action observation are often employed in therapeutic settings for patients with hemiplegia or other conditions that prevent actual movements. Decoding physiological signals during the imagination process plays a role in facilitating rehabilitation. However, the role of guided motor imagery in the imagination process has not been well studied. In this study, we compared the activation levels of oxygenated hemoglobin, the changes of neural activities' power in terms of time and frequency, and the differences and similarities of neural activations in the cortex area across seven different motor tasks under four conditions: motor execution (ME), MI, picture-guided motor imagery (PGMI) and video-guided motor imagery (VGMI). These findings demonstrate that although guided motor imagery (GMI) does not ease imagination tasks according to participant feedback, GMI reliably recruits mirror neurons during imagination when analyzing fNIRS and EEG signals. The results highlight that GMI has the potential to enrich BCI-based rehabilitation protocols for effectiveness enhancement.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society

papers.title: Participant-Disjoint EEG Decoding of Instructed Respiratory Conditions Using a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer.
papers.abstract: Fine-grained classification of instructed respiratory conditions from non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) remains challenging because of low signal-to-noise ratio and substantial inter-participant variability. This study proposes a Deep Spatio-Respiratory Transformer (DSRT) for EEG-based classification of instructed respiratory conditions. DSRT integrates differential entropy (DE) and normalized power-ratio (NPR) features, squeeze-and-excitation-based feature recalibration, a four-layer feature-token Transformer encoder, and auxiliary nasal/oral pathway supervision. The final task comprised eight respiratory-condition classes. The framework was evaluated using 64-channel EEG from 13 unique participants contributing 21 recording sessions. A fixed-count window-selection strategy was used to equalize the number of retained EEG windows across classes, and model evaluation was performed using participant-disjoint outer folds. Primary architecture comparisons and feature-representation analyses were conducted using participant-level performance summaries. At the participant level, DSRT achieved an Accuracy of 0.7429 ± 0.0492. Compared with EEG Conformer, the strongest matched-input comparison architecture, DSRT improved Accuracy and Macro-F1 by 3.78 and 3.79 percentage points, respectively. Architectural ablation showed the largest performance reduction after removal of the Transformer encoder, while participant-level feature-sensitivity analysis showed that the combined DE-NPR representation outperformed either feature family alone. DSRT contained 1.297 million parameters and achieved a median window-to-prediction latency of 3.825 ms. Duration-matched analysis further identified spatially heterogeneous EEG differences associated with instructed nasal and oral breathing. DSRT provides a participant-disjoint framework for fine-grained classification of EEG patterns associated with instructed respiratory conditions while retaining millisecond-scale inference. The findings support the utility of hybrid spectral representations and feature-token dependency modeling.
papers.journal: IEEE transactions on neural systems and rehabilitation engineering : a publication of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society

papers.title: Trait and daily self-compassion in relation to daily stress, eating behaviours and sleep: a daily diary study.
papers.abstract: Trait self-compassion is consistently associated with reduced stress and health-promoting behaviours. This study examined whether trait and state-like daily self-compassion played similar roles in relation to daily stress and health behaviours, and whether they moderated the associations between daily stress and daily health behaviours. A sample of 138 individuals completed baseline measures of trait self-compassion and eating styles, followed by a 7-day daily diary in which daily self-compassion, stress, eating, and sleep were assessed. Trait self-compassion was found to be positively associated with daily self-compassion. Trait self-compassion was also associated with uncontrolled, emotional, and intuitive eating styles. Multilevel modelling indicated that trait self-compassion was related to lower daily total snacking and better sleep outcomes, including reduced pre-sleep arousal and morning tiredness. At a daily level, self-compassion was associated with greater vegetable consumption, fewer hassles, more uplifts but poorer sleep quality. Finally, trait self-compassion moderated the relationship between daily stress and total snacking, such that individuals higher in self-compassion reported less snacking on stressful days. These findings extend existing knowledge by highlighting distinct associations of trait and daily self-compassion with daily stress, eating behaviours and sleep, and suggest that future research should further examine their potential roles in daily stress-health behaviour processes.

papers.title: Prefrontal Activation and Cognitive Heterogeneity in Pediatric Sleep-Disordered Breathing.
papers.abstract: Activation of the prefrontal cortex during attention and executive-function tasks can moderate associations between sleep-disordered breathing (SDB) symptoms and parent-reported behavior. However, conventional severity measures do not explain why cognitive outcomes vary among children with SDB. To assess whether prefrontal cortex (PFC) activity, reflecting attention and impulse control, is associated with SDB severity and cognition, and whether it distinguishes children whose cognition diverges from their SDB severity. This cross-sectional study included patients aged 5 to 11 years who were referred for evaluation of SDB at 2 academic pediatric otolaryngology centers from January 2024 to March 2026. Patients with neuromuscular disorders, prior airway surgery, continuous positive airway pressure treatment, sickle cell disease, stimulant use, or developmental delay were excluded. SDB severity measured by the Pediatric Sleep-Related Breathing Disorders Questionnaire, Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI), and oxygen saturation (SpO2) nadir. PFC activation measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) during a computer-based go or no-go task in which children respond to frequent cues and withhold responses to infrequent ones. Parent-reported executive function (Behavior Rating Inventory of Executive Function) and cognition (US National Institutes of Health [NIH] Toolbox Cognition Battery), and their associations with PFC activation. Linear mixed-effects models with false discovery rate (FDR) correction tested associations and moderation effects. Among 284 children (mean [SD] age, 7.9 [1.8] years; 130 [45.8%] female), 237 (83.5%) were at high risk for SDB. The mean (SD) AHI was 11.7 (14.5) events per hour and SpO2 nadir was 86.4% (8.2%). Higher AHI was associated with greater left dorsolateral PFC activation (oxyhemoglobin: β, 0.08; 95% CI, 0.03 to 0.12; deoxyhemoglobin: β, -0.07; 95% CI, -0.11 to -0.03), and lower SpO2 nadir was associated with greater activation (β, 0.14; 95% CI, 0.06 to 0.23). Greater activation in the right dorsolateral PFC was associated with worse parent-reported executive function after FDR correction. No severity measure was directly associated with NIH Toolbox performance after correction. However, PFC activation moderated the SDB severity-cognition association: children with greater activation maintained comparable performance despite more severe SDB. In this cross-sectional study, task-related PFC activation was associated with SDB severity and moderated the severity-cognition association. fNIRS may help identify children whose cognitive profiles deviate from conventional severity metrics, thereby supporting individualized cognitive risk assessment.

papers.title: Understanding the Complexity of Athlete Sleep: A Systems Approach to Modelling the Athlete Sleep Environment.
papers.abstract: Athlete sleep can be disrupted by sport- and non-sport-related factors. However, the interactions of these sleep-related factors are not well understood. Systems science approaches, such as causal loop diagramming (CLD), provide an opportunity to map these interactions. This project aimed to (1) develop a CLD of the athlete sleep system describing the interacting variables, (2) identify feedback loops and potential leverage points to optimise athlete sleep, and (3) demonstrate the applicability of a CLD to guide the development of a sleep monitoring framework. A systems-based model of athlete sleep was developed using CLD, informed by existing literature and refined through a consensus process involving ten subject matter experts (nine from Australia, one from the USA). The model was then interrogated using network analysis to identify key variables based on their position and connectivity within the system. These findings informed the development of a generic sleep monitoring framework. The CLD comprised 48 variables and 120 relationships across four domains: travel demands, behavioural and lifestyle factors, athlete condition and readiness, and resourcing and scheduling constraints. Overall, 12 key variables were identified, with hours of travel, number of time zones crossed, dose of caffeine, and amount of resources or expenditure available being the most connected upstream variables. Level of pre-sleep arousal, sleep opportunity, travel fatigue, and level of performance received the greatest number of incoming relationships, representing points at which multiple pathways converge. Physical condition, level of performance, quality of diet, and importance of competition most frequently linked different quadrants of the system. These variables informed a three-tier monitoring framework capturing upstream determinants and downstream consequences of sleep. According to the CLD, sleep health in athletes extends beyond an individual behaviour issue and is influenced by the structure and functioning of sport systems. Interactions among travel demands, physical readiness, behavioural and lifestyle factors, and organisational constraints sustain athlete sleep health over time. Consequently, meaningful improvements in sleep health are likely to arise from both system-level interventions and individual behaviour change strategies.

papers.title: Inflammatory masquerade features in adult-onset CLN-associated retinal degeneration in a multiethnic Asian cohort.
papers.abstract: To describe the clinical, imaging, and genetic features of non-syndromic neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis (NCL)-associated retinal degeneration in a multi-ethnic Asian cohort, with particular emphasis on cases that were initially considered in the differential diagnosis of non-neoplastic uveitis masquerade syndromes. This retrospective case series reviewed seven unrelated Singaporean patients (Chinese and Indian ancestry) with genetically confirmed CLN-associated inherited retinal degeneration. Clinical presentation, inflammatory features, longitudinal multimodal imaging, electrophysiology, and molecular findings were analyzed. Symptom onset ranged from 18 to 54 years. Presenting symptoms included "blurred vision/floaters (n = 3)", "nyctalopia (n = 3)", and "hemeralopia (n = 1)". Five patients presented with active ocular inflammation, such as anterior chamber and vitreous cells and retinal vasculitis. Notably, the other two patients (harboring CLN2 and CLN3 variants) did not show overt anterior or posterior segment inflammation; however, their striking structural and imaging similarities to inflammatory retinopathies prompted their inclusion in the masquerade differential. Across all seven patients, serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) revealed relentless outer retinal atrophy and loss of the ellipsoid zone. One of the five patients received corticosteroid and immunosuppressive therapy but showed only a limited response, whereas the remaining four patients responded favourably to topical, periocular, or oral corticosteroids. During a follow-up of 2.7-33.1 years, median best-corrected visual acuity declined to logMAR 1.90. Systemic health remained stable without neurological symptoms, except for one CLN2-associated case developing adult-onset neurosensory hearing loss. Pathogenic variants in CLN1, CLN2, CLN3, CLN5, and CLN7 were identified through genetic testing. CLN-associated disease accounted for 1.1% of the inherited retinal disease families in the cohort. Retinal degeneration associated with CLN1, CLN5, and CLN7 variants frequently presented with intraocular inflammation (ranging from anterior to panuveitis) in our cohort. Yet even patients without obvious inflammatory signs experienced a relentless retinal decline that closely mimicked the structural damage seen in severe posterior uveitis. These findings highlight why early genetic testing is so crucial when working up atypical, symmetrical posterior uveitis or suspected masquerade syndromes.
papers.journal: Journal of ophthalmic inflammation and infection

papers.title: Effect of remote patient monitoring on PAP adherence and patient-reported outcomes in obstructive sleep apnea: a comparative study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common condition, and positive airway pressure (PAP) is the standard therapy; however, its effectiveness depends on adherence. Remote patient monitoring (RPM) may improve PAP adherence, but evidence remains limited. We conducted a prospective, open-label, active-comparator, randomized trial comparing an RPM program with standard of care (SOC) in PAP-naive adults (≥ 18 years) with OSA who owned a smartphone. Participants were randomized 1:1 to SOC (PAP therapy with a standard coaching program) or RPM (PAP therapy monitored through a web-based application with coaching). The primary endpoint was Medicare-defined PAP adherence (> 4 h of use on > 70% of nights during a consecutive 30-day period within the first 90 days). Secondary endpoints included nights with elevated mask leak, patient-reported sleep measures, and patient satisfaction (Likert scale), with Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment for multiple comparisons. Given the pragmatic sample size, the study was designed to estimate between-arm differences rather than to test superiority with conventional power. The 196 participants (98 per arm) were 65% male, with a median (interquartile range) age of 51 (41-62) years and body mass index of 32 (29-37) kg/m². Medicare-defined PAP adherence was 80.6% in the RPM group and 73.5% in the SOC group (difference 7.1% points; p = 0.308). At day 90, the RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak (median 11.2 vs. 14.5; unadjusted p = 0.009; adjusted p = 0.113) and a higher proportion of participants reporting the highest satisfaction with timeliness of support, the coaching program, and issue resolution (unadjusted p = 0.031-0.044). None of these differences remained significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons (all adjusted p ≥ 0.11). Because of the limited sample size, conclusions are primarily descriptive. Medicare-defined PAP adherence did not differ significantly between RPM and SOC. The RPM group had fewer nights with elevated mask leak and higher satisfaction scores, but these differences were not significant after adjustment for multiple comparisons and require confirmation in an adequately powered trial. Retrospectively registered on 20,250,919 at https//clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07182617.

papers.title: Overweight and Obesity and Associated Risk Factors in Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) are at increased risk of overweight and obesity, but data from low-and middle-income countries are limited. This study assessed the prevalence and factors associated with overweight/obesity among children with ASD attending a tertiary care centre. This cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2023 to March 2025 in a developmental paediatrics unit in South India. Children aged 2-18 y with DSM-5-diagnosed ASD were consecutively recruited. Standardized anthropometry was performed, and BMI classified using age-appropriate criteria. Sociodemographic, clinical, dietary, feeding, lifestyle, and screen-related data were collected. All children underwent detailed multidisciplinary assessment. Overweight and obesity were combined for analysis. A multivariable logistic regression model was developed using clinically relevant variables and those showing evidence of univariate association, followed by backward likelihood-ratio elimination. Among 250 children with ASD, 47 (18.8%) had overweight/obesity. Of the children with overweight/obesity, 76.6% were aged >60 mo (36/47). In multivariable analysis, increasing age (adjusted OR [aOR] 1.028, 95% CI 1.013-1.044), higher ScreenQ score (aOR 1.092, 95% CI 1.004-1.188), higher BAMBI score (aOR 1.059, 95% CI 1.009-1.111), and frequent junk food consumption (aOR 2.801, 95% CI 1.166-6.729) were independently associated with overweight/obesity. Developmental quotients, autism severity, parental BMI, physical activity, sleep, and antipsychotic medication use were not significantly associated. Nearly one in five children with ASD were overweight or obese. Screen exposure, feeding difficulties, and frequent junk food intake were independently associated with excess weight, highlighting potentially modifiable targets for early family-centred interventions.

papers.title: Long-term benefits of early obstructive sleep apnea treatment in infants with Down syndrome.
papers.abstract: The Respire-21 study found that early obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) diagnosis and treatment is associated with improved neurocognitive and behavioral outcomes in infants with Down syndrome (DS) followed from 6 to 36 months of age (screened group) versus a control group receiving standard care at 36 months of age (standard care group). This follow-up study assessed whether these benefits persisted at 60 months of age and whether early OSA treatment influenced language and communication outcomes. Children from the initial study diagnosed with and treated for OSA underwent neurocognitive assessment at 60 months of age using the Griffiths Scales of Child Development, Third Edition (Griffiths III); the Vineland Adaptive Behavior Scales, Second Edition (VABS-II); and in-laboratory polysomnography. Twenty-four screened group and 13 standard care group children were included. The between-group difference in Griffiths III Global Quotient of Development favored the screened group but was not statistically significant (3.9 [standard error 2.8]; p = 0.130). The screened group scored significantly better on the Griffiths III Foundations of Learning (p = 0.014) and Personal-Social-Emotional (p = 0.019) domains, and on the VABS-II global composite score (p = 0.007), Daily Living Skills (p = 0.004), and Socialization (p = 0.005) domains. No significant benefit was observed for language or communication outcomes. Long-term neurocognitive benefits of early OSA screening and treatment were observed in infants with DS at 60 months of age, particularly for daily functioning and socialization. Registered at ClinicalTrials.gov under registration number NCT03210675 (registration date: 2017-07-05). Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is very frequent in infants with Down syndrome (DS). Early diagnosis and treatment of OSA is associated with significant improvement of neurocognitive outcomes and behavior at 36 months of age compared to no systematic evaluation of OSA. This study showed perduring benefits of early OSA interventions (at 60 months of age) compared with children receiving diagnosis and treatment later, i.e., after 36 months of age. Guidelines should be adapted to favor early interventions for OSA if diagnosed.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical sleep medicine : JCSM : official publication of the American Academy of Sleep Medicine

papers.title: Brainhack Rome 2025: connecting the dots between structure and function.
papers.abstract: Brainhack events provide a bottom-up approach to tackle challenges in neuroscience. In 2025, the Enrico Fermi Research Center in Rome hosted its first Brainhack, with the goal of fostering interdisciplinary collaborations bringing together the physics and neuroscience perspectives on the study of brain structure and function. Structured in four days, it gave the chance to the participants to propose their own idea and shape a project based on it, leading to six research avenues: the combination of X-ray imaging and diffusion MRI algorithms to pioneer ultra-high-resolution tractography; multivariate approaches to study the shared factors between brain metabolism and microstructure estimated from MRI data; development of transfer entropy analysis-based tools for effective connectivity estimation in fMRI data; identification of brain states through Markov models; deep learning approaches to predict task EEG time courses; multi-scale network models to study functional and cerebrovascular data. Each project led to promising results and marked the beginning of new collaborations.
authors: Tiago da Silva Alves de Nogueira Simões

papers.title: Behavioral, biochemical, histological, and electrophysiological changes following intracerebral injection of bone marrow stem cell-derived exosomes in male rat models of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Recently, researchers have been exploring how exosomes can help treat neurodegenerative diseases, such as Alzheimer's disease (AD), has attracted considerable attention. This study aimed to investigate behavioral, biochemical, histological, and electrophysiological changes following the administration of bone marrow stem cell-derived exosomes (Exo-BMSCs) in AD model rats. Animals were divided into control, Lesion (Lesion, Lesion + saline), and treatment (Lesion + BMSCs, Lesion + Exo-BMSCs) groups. BMSCs were extracted from the bone marrow of newborn rats. Exosomes were extracted from the BMSCs culture medium using a chemical kit. Saline, BMSCs, and Exo-BMSCs were injected bilaterally into the nucleus of Meynert (NBM) one week after electrical lesion. 28 days after injection, behavioral, electrophysiological, and histological changes, as well as ACh and BDNF expression levels in the hippocampus, were evaluated. Electrical lesion of the NBM caused a significant decrease in passive avoidance memory retrieval, a significant decrease in ACh and BDNF levels, changes in EEG wave frequencies in the hippocampus, and histological changes in the NBM, similar to those observed in AD. On the other hand, injection of BMSCs and Exo-BMSCs into the NBM significantly improved passive avoidance memory, an increase in BDNF levels, an increase in power of gamma waves, and improved histological changes compared to the Lesion groups. The increase in power of gamma waves was significant only in the Exo-BMSC-treated group. Injection of BMSCs and Exo-BMSCs into the NBM can significantly improve disease symptoms. This improvement was more pronounced in the Exo-BMSCs-treated group. The concurrent increase in BDNF suggests that this neurotrophin contributes to the observed effects.

papers.title: Cardiac regulatory and circadian gene expression and antioxidant enzyme activities in cold-exposed Daurian ground squirrels.
papers.abstract: The Daurian ground squirrel (Spermophilus dauricus) is a typical hibernating mammal, exhibiting tolerance to low ambient temperatures. To elucidate the cardiac physiological adaptation mechanisms of animals to cold exposure, the present study investigated the effects of continuous 6-day cold exposure (5 ± 1 °C) on the expression of cardiac functional genes, Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase, and antioxidant enzyme activity in summer-active Daurian ground squirrels. Cold exposure significantly reduced the mRNA expression of nNOS, eNOS, Adora1, Adora2A, and Adrb1, while increasing that of Chrm2. It also significantly downregulated the expression of the circadian genes Clock, Cry2, and Per1-3, whereas Cry1 expression was upregulated. The cardiac Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase activity was decreased, while activities of T-AOC, SOD, and CAT in the heart were enhanced, and MDA content increased. These findings suggest that cold exposure may affect cardiac function via circadian genes, NO signaling, and adenosine/adrenergic/cholinergic regulation, while minimizing ion transport energy expenditure and enhancing antioxidant defense.
papers.journal: Journal of comparative physiology. B, Biochemical, systemic, and environmental physiology

papers.title: From cave adaptation to ageing resilience: the Mexican cavefish Astyanax mexicanus.
papers.abstract: The Mexican cavefish, Astyanax mexicanus, is a powerful evolutionary model for investigating how adaptation to extreme environments reshapes vertebrate physiology. Multiple cave populations have independently evolved under subterranean conditions, acquiring traits including insulin resistance, persistent hyperglycaemia, increased adiposity, altered sleep patterns, hypoxia tolerance and extensive metabolic reprogramming. Despite these differences, cavefish exhibit lifespans comparable to those of surface fish, while selected traits, including fertility and locomotor performance, appear to be better preserved with age. These observations challenge the assumption that persistent metabolic dysfunction necessarily entails accelerated functional decline and raise the possibility that cavefish have evolved mechanisms of ageing resilience. This narrative review examines evidence linking cave adaptation to biological processes relevant to ageing, focusing on nutrient sensing, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, redox homeostasis and immune regulation. Rather than eliminating metabolic stress, cave-associated adaptations may buffer some of its downstream consequences, preserving selected physiological functions. Evidence is evaluated within the framework of the hallmarks of ageing, considering genomic instability, telomere dynamics, deregulated nutrient sensing, mitochondrial dysfunction and chronic inflammation, while identifying major knowledge gaps regarding epigenetic alterations, loss of proteostasis, macroautophagy, cellular senescence, stem-cell exhaustion, altered intercellular communication and dysbiosis. The available evidence supports A. mexicanus as a comparative model for investigating how chronic environmental and metabolic stress can be uncoupled from selected aspects of functional decline. Distinguishing delayed ageing from enhanced tolerance or compensation in response to accumulated damage will be essential to establish the extent and mechanisms of ageing resilience in this species.

papers.title: Pharmacology Update: Pruritus in Palliative Care With Focus on Naltrexone.
papers.abstract: BackgroundPruritus is a common and often distressing symptom in palliative care, affecting a significant fraction of patients and significantly impairing sleep, mood, and quality of life. Common etiologies include chronic kidney disease, cholestatic liver disease, hematologic malignancies, solid tumors, medication-related syndromes, and paraneoplastic processes. Conventional treatments, including antihistamines, antidepressants, gabapentinoids, ondansetron, and ultraviolet-B phototherapy, are frequently limited by adverse effects, cost, or practicality in seriously ill patients.ObjectiveTo review the pathophysiology of pruritus relevant to palliative care and evaluate the emerging role of naltrexone as a therapeutic option for refractory pruritus.MethodsNarrative review of the literature addressing the mechanisms of pruritus, current treatment approaches, and clinical evidence supporting the use of naltrexone across various pruritic conditions encountered in palliative medicine.ResultsIncreasing evidence implicates dysregulation of the endogenous opioid system in the pathogenesis of several forms of chronic pruritus. As a competitive opioid receptor antagonist, naltrexone may mitigate "itch" through μ-opioid receptor blockade and restoration of opioid signaling balance. The strongest evidence supports its use in cholestatic pruritus, where randomized placebo-controlled trials demonstrated significant reductions in symptom severity with 50 mg daily dosing. Evidence in uremic pruritus is mixed, with some studies showing benefit and others finding no superiority over placebo. Case reports and small series suggest potential efficacy in malignancy-associated pruritus, polycythemia vera, and selected dermatologic disorders. Limitations include contraindication in patients receiving opioid therapy, potential precipitation of withdrawal, and adverse effects such as nausea, gastrointestinal distress, dizziness, fatigue, and sleep disturbance.ConclusionsNaltrexone represents a mechanistically rational and potentially effective option for selected patients with refractory pruritus in palliative care. Current evidence is most compelling for cholestatic pruritus, while data for other etiologies remain limited and heterogeneous. Larger prospective studies are needed to define optimal dosing strategies, identify patients most likely to benefit, and better characterize its role in opioid-exposed palliative care populations.
papers.journal: The American journal of hospice & palliative care

papers.title: Subjective Age Discrepancy Associates With Sleep Quality in a Large Longitudinal Sample of Middle-Aged and Older Adults.
papers.abstract: While age is typically measured in chronological terms, subjective age has also been shown to be clinically relevant. Given the clinical importance of subjective age discrepancy (the distinction between chronological and subjective age), we aimed to examine whether it was associated with another important aspect of health, sleep quality, among middle-aged and older British adults. Data from the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing was analysed. We used a longitudinal approach involving a primary test sample (N = 11,050) and an independent replication sample (N = 1800). Subjective sleep quality, sleep duration and frequency of difficulties falling asleep, staying asleep or experiencing unrefreshing sleep were self-reported and subjective age discrepancy was derived from items regarding chronological age and subjective age. Regression analysis was conducted cross-sectionally within a wave of data collection and longitudinally between two data waves separated by 4 years. Better sleep quality (β = -0.11) and longer sleep duration (β = -0.03) were associated cross-sectionally with 'younger' subjective age discrepancy and unrefreshing sleep (β = -0.12) emerged as the sleep factor most strongly associated with subjective age discrepancy. In the test sample, but not the replication sample, sleep quality had interactions with chronological age, sex and the presence of long-term illness in its association with subjective age discrepancy. In longitudinal analysis, subjective age discrepancy was a predictor of sleep quality 4 years later, and subjective age discrepancy predicted sleep quality both cross-sectionally and longitudinally. Sleep quality and subjective age discrepancy emerge as potential sites for intervention to influence each other for enhancement of quality of life in middle-to-older aged adults.

papers.title: Childhood Trauma and APOEε4 Are Associated With Patterns of Developmental Frontal Alpha Connectivity, Posttraumatic Stress, and Alcohol-Related Outcomes.
papers.abstract: Childhood trauma affects neurodevelopment and lifelong risk for posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) and alcohol use disorder (AUD). Changes in brain structures and function are observed in young carriers of APOEε4, the genetic factor most associated with Alzheimer's disease. Longitudinal studies of APOEε4, childhood trauma, and neural connectivity in adolescence have not been explored. We studied 837 trauma-exposed participants (53% female) from the Collaborative Study on the Genetics of Alcoholism prospective sample, using latent growth curve models to assess associations of childhood trauma and APOEε4 on repeated measures of frontal alpha EEG coherence (EEGc) throughout adolescence and young adulthood. Young adult AUD and PTSD symptoms were also examined. Results indicate childhood sexual assaultive trauma (CSAT) and APOEε4 are linked to neural connectivity, with effects differing by brain region and direction. CSAT was associated with a higher EEGc baseline but less growth in three EEGc pairs, while APOEε4 associated with lower left frontocentral (LFC) EEGc baseline and higher slope. EEGc patterns and symptoms of PTSD and AUD were robustly associated. A significant interaction between CSAT-by-APOEε4 interaction also emerged, such that among APOEε4 carriers, childhood sexual assaultive trauma was associated with higher baseline PFI and diminished growth in PFI and LFC EEGc. No significant direct links between APOEε4 and PTSD or AUD were observed. Findings highlight how EEGc may help explain connections between genetics, trauma, and psychopathology, guiding at-risk group identification and informing prevention strategies.

papers.title: A phenome-wide association study of externalizing polygenic risk in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) study.
papers.abstract: Externalizing disorders encompass a range of disinhibited behaviors that typically manifest in youth and are linked with adverse psychological and social outcomes. Polygenic liability to externalizing behaviors has been associated with psychiatric and disease phenotypes in adults. Identifying correlates of genetic risk in youth-prior to the emergence of more impairing manifestations of externalizing behaviors (e.g. substance use disorders)-could improve our etiological understanding and inform targeted prevention efforts. We conducted a phenome-wide association study (PheWAS) to test whether externalizing (EXT) polygenic scores (PGS) were associated with up to 1,697 psychosocial, behavioral, environmental, and health-related phenotypes among youth of European-like genetic ancestry. PheWAS data came from the baseline (n = 4,931, mean age = 9.93 ± 0.63 years, 46.9% female) and two-year follow-up (n = 4,507, 12.02 ± 0.66 years, 47.0% female) data collection waves of the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development StudySM (ABCD Study®). Secondary analyses examined within-family effects and moderation by biological sex. EXT PGS was associated with 268 and 352 phenotypes at baseline and follow-up, respectively, following Bonferroni correction at each wave. The strongest associations were observed with externalizing behaviors, screen time/media use, caffeine consumption, sleep disturbances, and poor school performance. Effects were attenuated by 59%-64% within family, on average, with five predominantly externalizing phenotypes remaining significantly associated with within-family PGS. There was limited evidence of moderation by biological sex. These results broadly characterize the early phenotypic correlates of an externalizing polygenic score and can be used to generate hypotheses about phenotypes that might represent mechanisms or future prevention targets.

papers.title: Validating the Updated Family Nutrition and Physical Activity Survey in Spanish in the Dominican Context.
papers.abstract: To address the pediatric obesity pandemic disproportionately affecting Latino children, particularly in the Caribbean, this study developed and validated a culturally tailored Spanish version of the Family Nutrition Physical Activity (FNPA) instrument for the Dominican context. Through a multi-step iterative process involving bilingual medical professionals, ten healthcare providers, and 50 guardians of children aged 6-12, the tool underwent rigorous translation and cognitive validation. Participants found the Spanish FNPA easy to understand and culturally relevant. Essential modifications included adding local examples-such as specific sugar-sweetened beverages-and guidance on healthy sleep practices to ensure accurate responses. Ultimately, the study confirmed that the translated FNPA is culturally appropriate for Dominican families and providers. These findings support the use of the instrument in the Dominican Republic and suggest that future research should explore its applicability in other Spanish-speaking regions to compare behavioral trends across diverse settings.
papers.journal: Hispanic health care international : the official journal of the National Association of Hispanic Nurses

papers.title: Association of Lactate-to-Albumin Ratio With 28-Day Mortality in Critically Ill Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Cohort Study Based on the MIMIC-IV Database.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is not uncommon among critically ill patients, especially in those with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure. Its high mortality rate remains a major challenge in the intensive care setting. The frequent apnea and respiratory failure during sleep in OSA patients, along with the intermittent hypoxemia caused by it, are accompanied by a series of systemic pathological and physiological changes. Metabolic imbalance is a key characteristic of the underlying pathological mechanism of this disease. However, the association between lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and the prognosis of OSA patients remains to be fully elucidated. To date, a paucity of studies has evaluated the prognostic capabilities of these indicators. The majority of these studies have focused on the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), and the results are contradictory, insufficient to fully clarify their clinical significance. Relying solely on lactate may not fully reflect patients' physiological conditions, whereas integrating LAR can provide a more comprehensive and accurate description of the metabolic state. This study aims to explore the relationship between LAR and 28-day mortality rates in ICU patients with OSA, using data from the MIMIC-IV database. Patients diagnosed with OSA were selected from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (v.2.2) database, identified by specific ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes (detailed in the Methods section). To assess the predictive power of LAR, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival curve analysis, logistic regression analysis, and subgroup analysis were employed. LAR was analyzed both as a categorical variable (based on the optimal cutoff) and as a continuous variable. The sample population comprised 807 patients diagnosed with OSA who were admitted to the intensive care unit for the first time. The 28-day mortality rate was 20.44%. The area under the ROC curve (AUC) for LAR was 0.730 (95% CI: 0.686-0.772), which was comparable with OASIS (0.736; 95% CI: 0.695-0.776) and superior to SOFA (0.637; 95% CI: 0.591-0.683; DeLong test p = 0.500). The optimal cutoff value for LAR was 0.791. The high-LAR group demonstrated a poor prognosis in the K-M analysis (p < 0.001). Multivariate logistic regression demonstrated a significant association between LAR and unfavorable outcomes, with an odds ratio (OR) of 3.00 (95% CI: 1.83-4.90, p < 0.001) when analyzed as a dichotomous variable, and an OR of 1.52 per unit increase (95% CI: 1.27-1.82, p < 0.001) when analyzed as a continuous variable. Subgroup analysis revealed no statistically significant interaction between LAR and any subgroup (p for interaction: 0.052-0.906). LAR is a rational and easily accessible biomarker that is significantly associated with 28-day mortality in ICU patients with OSA. These findings are only applicable to OSA patients who received lactate and albumin testing during ICU admission, and the results cannot be generalized to the entire population of ICU patients with OSA.

papers.title: Tetramelic Monodactyly With Neonatal Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Congenital limb defects are etiologically heterogeneous congenital malformations, with genetic causes being one of the major contributors. We report a neonate with limb anomalies and severe encephalopathy in whom rapid trio whole-genome sequencing identified a pathogenic duplication at 10q24.31q24.32. A near-term male neonate presented with bilateral radial and tibial ray aplasia, with preserved ulnar and fibular elements, resulting in tetramelic monodactyly of the fifth digits. Family history revealed an apparent autosomal dominant pattern, with the patient's father and older sister similarly affected. In the first days of life, the patient developed unexplained apnea, respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation, and severe diffuse encephalopathy on continuous EEG monitoring. Brain MRI, head ultrasound, and metabolic workup were unremarkable. Echocardiography showed normal cardiac anatomy. Trio rapid whole-genome sequencing demonstrated a 10q24 duplication, a locus previously associated with split-hand/foot malformation. This genetic variant in this family leads to tetramelic monodactyly of the fifth digits across at least two generations.

papers.title: Single-nucleus atlas of circadian transcription in mouse liver and skeletal muscle.
Working memory gating across sensory modalities reveals modality-specific maintenance mechanisms.
papers.abstract: The flexible resolution of the conflict between updating and maintenance demands in working memory is thought to rely on a selective gating mechanism. While gating of visual information has been extensively studied, gating of multisensory information remains poorly understood. We addressed this gap by contrasting task performance and accompanying neuro-oscillatory modulations across a purely visual and two audiovisual variants of a working memory gating task. Task-dependent performance differences emerged specifically for gate closing. Across tasks, gate closing was consistently associated with alpha band activity modulations supporting the integration of task-relevant information and beta band activity modulations controlling the reconfiguration of the gate state, while theta band activity modulations were overall negligible. However, the functional localization and relative magnitude of these oscillatory modulations varied between tasks. Together, our findings suggest that working memory gating is not amodal, but that maintenance processes in particular are shaped by the sensory context.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in Saudi otolaryngology research: a scoping review of the current landscape, gaps, and future directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in otolaryngology, but the extent and focus of AI research in Saudi Arabia remain unclear. This scoping review mapped the available evidence and identified key research themes and knowledge gaps. A scoping review was conducted following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and the Saudi Medical Journal archive were searched for studies published between January 2019 and April 2026. Eligible studies investigated AI applications or clinician perspectives within Saudi otolaryngology. The evidence was mapped across major otolaryngology domains, including cochlear implantation and hearing, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, head and neck oncology, surgical and other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea, AI education and implementation, and AI-assisted patient education. The searches identified 2,925 database records, four records from other sources and seven records from an updated search and expert suggestions; thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria. The evidence covered AI awareness and education, large language model (LLM)-based patient education, cochlear implantation, rhinology and skull base surgery, facial plastic surgery, laryngology and voice, and head and neck oncology; no eligible study addressed surgical or other ENT-related interventions for obstructive sleep apnoea. Clinicians were generally positive about AI, while clinical studies showed promising performance of AI models. LLM chatbots generally gave accurate postoperative advice, although, when validated tools were used, their responses were harder to read and less actionable than patient-education standards recommend. However, limited AI education, small or non-Saudi datasets, limited external validation, and implementation barriers remained important challenges. AI research in Saudi otolaryngology remains limited but is expanding across several clinical domains. Future research should prioritise Saudi-specific datasets, multicentre clinical validation, structured AI education, rigorous bilingual (Arabic and English) evaluation of LLM-generated patient information, and safe integration of AI into clinical practice in line with Saudi Vision 2030.

papers.title: Reproductive Factors and Pain Among Middle-Aged and Older Chinese Women: Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Evidence from CHARLS.
papers.abstract: To examine reproductive factors and pain in middle-aged and older Chinese women. We used CHARLS data, combining the core survey with the Life History reproductive module. The cross-sectional analysis included 8532 women in 2018; the longitudinal analysis included 3856 women pain-free at the 2011 baseline with pain assessments in 2013, 2015, or 2018. The outcome was self-reported any pain, not clinically diagnosed chronic pain. Survey-weighted logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Menopause exposures were evaluated in a postmenopausal-baseline sensitivity analysis; musculoskeletal pain sensitivity analyses tested robustness. Cross-sectionally, three or more biological children (vs one, OR 1.30, 95% CI 1.06-1.61) and three or more miscarriages (vs none, OR 1.83, 95% CI 1.07-3.13) were associated with prevalent self-reported any pain in 2018. Longitudinally, 2743 women first reported pain during follow-up. Menarche after age 18 was associated with lower odds of first reported pain in the primary cumulative model (OR 0.66, 95% CI 0.49-0.87) and the discrete-time person-period analysis (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.61-0.92). Three or more miscarriages were associated with higher odds in the primary longitudinal model (OR 3.66, 95% CI 1.01-13.32) but were imprecise and not significant in the person-period analysis. Early menopause was associated with follow-up pain only in the postmenopausal-baseline sensitivity analysis (OR 1.61, 95% CI 1.08-2.40). Cross-sectional findings were supported by musculoskeletal pain sensitivity analyses. Later age at menarche was associated with lower odds of self-reported follow-up pain across two complete-case longitudinal modeling approaches, a signal that requires confirmation. Higher parity and multiple miscarriages were associated with prevalent pain cross-sectionally. The longitudinal signals for multiple miscarriages and early menopause were less robust and exploratory. Because the outcome was self-reported any pain rather than clinically diagnosed chronic pain, these associations are hypothesis-generating; prospective studies with standardized, chronic-pain-specific outcomes are needed.

papers.title: Tryptophan metabolism circadian regulation: clinical and pharmacological implications.
papers.abstract: Circadian clocks are endogenous systems that synchronize physiology and behavior to the light-dark cycle, regulating sleep-wake timing, hormonal rhythms, metabolism and immunity. Among metabolic pathways tightly linked to circadian rhythm, tryptophan (Trp) metabolism occupies a central position because its catabolism through the kynurenine (Kyn) pathway, the serotonin (5-HT)-melatonin pathway and the microbiota-derived indole-AhR pathway, produce molecules endowed with significant neuro-modulatory and immunoregulatory activities and directly involved in circadian regulation. Emerging evidence supports a bidirectional relationship between the clock system and Trp metabolism. The molecular clock regulates expression and activity of key Trp enzymes, creating time-of-day variation in Trp flux, Kyn-Trp ratio, serotonin/melatonin synthesis and AhR ligands availability. Conversely, Trp-derived metabolites in turn modulate clock function and downstream physiology, such as diurnal variations in metabolism and immune response. Here we discuss recent studies highlighting how this interplay has important pathophysiological implications and disruption of Trp metabolism oscillatory pattern influences our susceptibility to developing diseases, such as infectious, metabolic and neuropsychiatric diseases. Moreover, we highlight the importance of considering daily fluctuation when using these molecules as biomarkers and interpreting them in a clinical setting. Among circadian-based interventions, such as chronotherapy, light therapy or time-restricted feeding, we propose pharmacological targeting of Trp pathways or pharmacological use of Trp derivatives as a novel approach of circadian medicine, able to improve clinical outcomes across various fields.

papers.title: The efficacy of NMDA receptor antagonists in neuropsychiatric and non-motor symptoms of Parkinson's disease: a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) involves significant non-motor symptoms (NMS) linked to glutamate dysregulation. This review evaluates the efficacy of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor antagonists (memantine and amantadine) for treating NMS. A search was conducted in the databases PubMed and Cochrane Library (January 2000-September 2025) for controlled trials focusing on NMS in idiopathic PD. Two reviewers assessed bias using Cochrane RoB 2. Of 529 records, ten studies were included. Most exhibited a high risk of bias and heterogeneity. Memantine results were mixed: improvements in attention and behavioral symptoms were observed in PD dementia, but no benefit or worsened memory occurred in mild cognitive impairment. Memantine was beneficial for REM sleep behavior disorder. Extended-release amantadine improved sleepiness and mood but increased hallucinations and cognitive impairment. Evidence is limited by methodological flaws. While memantine offers selective benefits for PD dementia, amantadine carries notable cognitive risks. High-quality trials are essential to clarify therapeutic roles.

papers.title: PP2A-dependent downregulation of GABAB receptors modulates somatostatin interneurons function and plasticity.
papers.abstract: Cortical circuits require precise inhibitory and excitatory neurotransmission to encode information and prevent pathology. Metabotropic GABAB receptors (GABABRs) are key inhibitory regulators in mammalian neurons. In GABAergic interneurons (INs), GABABR activation reduces inhibition, leading to disinhibitory mechanisms. Hippocampal somatostatin-expressing (SST) INs provide feedback inhibition to distal dendrites of principal cells (PCs) and other INs. Plasticity of SST INs is well established to control hippocampal circuit function dependent on metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs) and GABABRs. Whether GABABRs regulate SST INs function over longer time scales and if this influences circuit function remains unclear. We combine quantitative freeze-fracture replica immunoelectron microscopy, ex vivo electrophysiology, and pharmacology to show that GABABR activation regulates long-term potentiation (LTP) of SST INs through protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A)-dependent loss of cell-surface GABABR, mGluR1α receptors, and Cav1.2 (L-type) Ca2+ channels. GABABR loss in SST INs shifts hippocampal activity toward greater plasticity of long-range inputs to CA1.

papers.title: Transforming neurophysiological data into measurable stress metric using machine learning-based stress quantification framework for smart factory workers.
papers.abstract: Mental stress is a common issue in demanding occupational setups, such as smart industrial settings, particularly when working with robots, being one of the primary reasons for decreased performance and productivity. Estimating and evaluating stress are critical for worker safety, performance, and overall well-being. A novel integrated framework is proposed in this research for continuous cognitive stress-level estimation that combines neuroimaging (EEG and fNIRS), gaze tracking and machine learning. A factory workers' stress assessment experiment is designed and implemented, which employs physiological, behavioral and subjective measures to assess mental stress from different perspectives. Physiological features extracted from multimodal neuroimaging data are used for training supervised classification and regression models, while gaze, behavioral, and subjective measures provide complementary evaluation of worker stress. To further optimize the pipeline, multiple feature selection algorithms are tested, followed by ensemble learning approaches, and the best model is chosen for continuous stress-level estimation. After implementing the novel stress quantification framework for the factory workers' stress assessment experiment, the ensemble learning approach produced the best results for both regression (RMSE: 10.86) and classification (accuracy: 84.1%) techniques using the STAI score as the target. The behavioral and subjective measures demonstrate the effect of varying process variables (light, noise, task speed, and complexity) during the experiment. Multimodal data, machine learning, and other computational approaches are integrated in this study to estimate continuous cognitive stress levels, utilizing the proposed framework presented in this research, thereby bridging the gap between research and practical application. The proposed multi-domain framework provides a promising solution for monitoring worker well-being in occupational settings.

papers.title: Altered Melatonin Secretion and Recurrent Sleep-Related Headache in a Patient With a Pineal Cyst: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Melatonin contributes to the circadian regulation of sleep and nociception, and disruption of its secretion has been implicated in headache disorders with nocturnal periodicity. The functional relevance of pineal cysts in this context remains poorly defined. A 23-year-old woman presented with a four-year history of stereotyped headaches occurring exclusively between 1:30 and 4:00 a.m. and awakening her from sleep. The attacks were occipital-suboccipital, pulsating and pressure-like, rated 7/10 in intensity, and accompanied by scalp allodynia, bilateral conjunctival hyperemia and lacrimation, mild nasal congestion, and restlessness. Neurologic examination and investigations for secondary causes were unremarkable. Serial brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated a benign-appearing pineal cyst measuring initially 21 × 11 × 10 mm, without hydrocephalus, obstruction of cerebrospinal fluid pathways, or aggressive radiologic features. Two melatonin measurements obtained at 3:00 a.m. were reduced at 14 and 16 pg/mL against a laboratory reference range of 40-80 pg/mL. Treatment with oral melatonin at 4 mg nightly reduced the headache symptoms by approximately 50% within four weeks. Increasing the dose to 8 mg nightly was followed by complete resolution within six weeks. After three months, the nocturnal melatonin concentration was 52 pg/mL, and the patient remained headache-free without reported adverse effects at the six-month follow-up. This case demonstrates a temporal association among nocturnal headaches, reduced nocturnal melatonin secretion, and improvement following melatonin supplementation. Although a single case cannot establish causality, assessment of circadian hormone secretion may be considered in selected patients with pineal lesions and strictly nocturnal headaches.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence in cardiovascular medicine: systematic review of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds considerable promise for improving cardiovascular care, but prior to widespread adoption, AI-powered tools require evaluation in randomized trials. We systematically reviewed the current evidence from randomized trials of AI tools in cardiovascular medicine. We conducted a systematic review of randomized trials comparing AI tools vs. standard care in cardiovascular medicine. PubMed, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Scopus, and the International Clinical Trials Registry Platform were searched from 1 January 2018, to 10 April 2026. Screening and full-text review were performed by three independent reviewers and risk of bias was assessed using the RoB 2 criteria. Of 11 151 identified records, 8599 remained after removal of duplicates. Following screening and full-text review, 25 trials met the eligibility criteria. These trials evaluated AI tools in acute cardiovascular care (n = 3), cardiac imaging (n = 6), decision support for medical therapy (n = 6), electrophysiology (n = 8), and interventional cardiology (n = 2). Nine trials were single-centre, and two were international. Seventeen trials (68%) reported positive results, defined by non-inferiority or superiority of the AI-based strategy. Overall risk of bias was rated as high or with some concerns in 84% of the included trials, and only 36% explicitly reported following the CONSORT-/SPIRIT-AI reporting guidelines. Evidence from randomized trials evaluating AI tools in cardiovascular medicine is limited, and most trials have a high risk of bias. Wider implementation of AI tools into practice requires robust, international, multi-centre randomized trials that evaluate patient-relevant outcomes, ensure external validity, and adhere to reporting guidelines. PROSPERO CRD420251019264.

papers.title: Advancing Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation for Depression: Novel Protocols, Precision Targeting, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) remains a significant global health challenge, with substantial limitations inherent in current pharmacotherapeutic and psychotherapeutic approaches. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) has emerged as a safe, effective, and non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, particularly for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). However, conventional rTMS is limited by long treatment duration and variable interindividual efficacy. This expert opinion examines recent advances in rTMS optimization strategies aimed at overcoming these limitations. Key areas of progress include the development of novel stimulation protocols such as theta-burst stimulation (TBS); accelerated regimens and priming TMS; the use of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-guided TMS; and the integration of closed-loop systems using real-time electroencephalography (EEG) or functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) feedback. Additionally, technological innovations, including robot-assisted TMS and wearable devices, promise to enhance targeting accuracy and treatment accessibility. Despite these developments, significant challenges impede clinical translation, including the high cost of personalized protocols, insufficient standardization and validation of novel approaches, and technical barriers to closed-loop implementation. Future efforts should focus on cost reduction, large-scale randomized controlled trials, biomarker development, and device portability. Ultimately, optimized rTMS shows significant potential to become a more efficient, precise, and accessible cornerstone of depression therapy.

papers.title: U-Shaped Associations Between Sleep Duration and Abdominal Obesity in Taiwanese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study was to investigate the association between sleep duraton and risk of abdominal obesity in Taiwanese adults, an issue of public health significance given the role of central obesity in increasing metabolic and cardiovascular risks. This was a cross-sectional study conducted on 58,238 adults age from 23 to 64 years old (male: 47.63%) who participated in Taiwan's National Physical Fitness Survey 2014-2015. Data from a standardized structured questionnaire and anthropometric measures were analyzed. Individuals' sleep duration was categorized as very short (≤5.0 hours), short (5.1-6.0 hours), optimal (6.1-7.0 hours), long (7.1-8.0 hours), or very long (>8.0 hours). Abdominal obesity was classified according to waist circumference (WC) ≥ 90 cm for men and WC ≥ 80 cm for women. Multiple logistic regression analyses, adjusted for demographic and lifestyle covariates, were performed to evaluate the risk factors for abdominal obesity. The multiple logistic regression, using the optimal sleep duration as a baseline, indicated significant associations between very short (OR = 1.14, 95% CI: 1.02-1.27), short (OR = 1.11, 95% CI: 1.04-1.19) and very long (OR = 1.09, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18) sleep durations and abdominal obesity after adjusting for potential confounding factors. Our findings suggest that subjects with shorter or longer sleep durations have a higher risk of abdominal obesity than those with optimal sleep durations.

papers.title: Expert opinion survey on the pharmacological treatment of insomnia in Japan (2025).
papers.abstract: Rapidly evolving insomnia management with orexin receptor antagonists (ORAs) has outpaced current clinical guidelines. This study aimed to provide a practical expert opinion reflecting specialists' collective experience to bridge the gap between existing recommendations and contemporary clinical practice in Japan. Cross-sectional web-based survey. A web-based questionnaire survey conducted in late 2025 targeted board-certified experts in clinical neuropsychopharmacology. Experts rated treatment options for 17 clinical scenarios using a nine-point Likert scale.
