Treatments were categorized as first-, second-, or third-line based on the 95% confidence interval (CI), with "treatments of choice" defined by ≥50% of respondents assigning the highest score. A total of 152 responses were analyzed (response rate: 43.4%). ORAs occupied central positions across nearly all scenarios. Lemborexant was the treatment of choice for both sleep initiation and maintenance, while suvorexant and daridorexant were also first-line options. When ORA monotherapy was insufficient, switching to another ORA was the preferred strategy. In contrast, most benzodiazepine receptor agonists were relegated to lower-line treatments, with eszopiclone remaining a notable exception as a second-line option. Regarding treatment duration, experts showed an increased tendency for continuing pharmacotherapy, particularly when clinical stability was incomplete or relapse risk was high. This opinion survey demonstrates a clear shift toward ORA-based strategies in Japan and a growing acceptance of ORA continuation based on clinical stability. While representing a lower evidence level than formal guidelines, these practice-based insights offer a valuable reference for pharmacological decision-making in real-world scenarios where high-level evidence is limited.

papers.title: Polysomnography Indicators Associated With Moderate Depression: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to use polysomnography (PSG) and clinical rating scales to evaluate sleep quality, sleep characteristics, and their associations in patients with moderate depression. A total of 52 patients with moderate depression and 21 healthy controls were enrolled. All participants underwent PSG and were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Differences in clinical characteristics between the two groups were analyzed. Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with moderate depression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the diagnostic performance of PSG indicators for moderate depression. Compared with healthy controls, patients with moderate depression exhibited significantly higher total PSQI scores and poorer objective sleep quality based on PSG measurements. Specifically, they had shorter total sleep time (TST), longer wake after sleep onset (WASO), lower sleep efficiency (SE), a higher percentage of wakefulness (W%), fewer rapid eye movement (REM) sleep cycles, and a higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) (all p < 0.05). Multivariate binary logistic regression analysis showed that each 1-point increase in the PSQI score was associated with a 6.66-fold increase in the odds of moderate depression (95% CI = 1.143-38.835, p = 0.035). The PSQI score showed excellent discriminative performance (AUC = 0.990, 95% CI: 0.974-1.000), whereas the univariate ROC results for age, ArI, REM cycle, and AHI should be interpreted cautiously as exploratory findings rather than evidence of independent predictive value. Patients with moderate depression exhibit poorer subjective and objective sleep quality than healthy individuals and demonstrate distinct polysomnographic characteristics.

papers.title: Breakage-Related Remanufacture of Mandibular Advancement Devices in Patients With Obstructive Sleep Apnea: A Retrospective Study of 219 Patients.
papers.abstract: Mandibular advancement devices (MADs) are used for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), but the frequency of new-device fabrication following breakage during treatment is uncertain. We analyzed 219 patients treated with a custom-made fixed-type MAD at a single center. The endpoint was the first documented new-device fabrication due to device breakage, across successive appliances if necessary, measured from the initial recorded fabrication date. The record term "repair" denoted new-device fabrication, whereas adjustment of an existing device was not an event. Dental-treatment and loss-related replacements did not end patient-level observation. For patients without a documented breakage event, absence of a return visit was assumed to mean no recorded event through March 31, 2025. Fifty-eight of 219 patients (26.5%) had a first breakage-related remanufacture; 161 were administratively censored. Two patients had an intervening new device for a non-device reason: one later had a breakage event and one did not. Median analytic observation time was 45.9 months (IQR 18.4-77.3; range 0.3-180.7). Estimated event-free survival at one and three years was 91.6% (95% CI 87.0-94.6) and 81.1% (95% CI 74.8-86.0), respectively. Actual last-contact dates and loss to clinical follow-up could not be determined. Breakage-related new-device fabrication was documented during MAD treatment. These patient-level estimates depend on an unverified assumption that patients who did not return had no recorded event; they do not describe the physical lifespan of a single appliance or treatment efficacy.

papers.title: Generative-augmented multimodal neuroaffective decoding for product evaluation: toward neurofeedback-driven human-in-the-loop co-design.
papers.abstract: Kansei engineering traditionally relies on self-reported evaluations of product impressions, which are susceptible to contextual influences, recall bias, and assessment timing. Multimodal psychophysiological measurements offer complementary insights into affective responses, but integrating heterogeneous signals with limited sample sizes remains challenging. This study proposes Generative-Augmented Multimodal Affective Fusion (GAMAF) to predict perceived attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness in product evaluation. GAMAF integrates feature-space conditional Wasserstein generative adversarial learning with gradient penalty (cWGAN-GP), cross-modal attention, graph-based interactions, and adaptive modality weighting. Fifty participants evaluated three automobile cockpit designs, yielding 150 participant-stimulus trials after multimodal quality control. Electroencephalography (EEG), eye tracking (ET), and peripheral physiological signals were integrated and evaluated using nested participant-wise cross-validation. GAMAF achieved mean outer-fold R² values of 0.810, 0.850, and 0.840 for attractiveness, innovativeness, and friendliness, respectively, each with a standard deviation of 0.016. These values exceeded those of the Multimodal Transformer baseline (0.75, 0.78, and 0.76, respectively). Across the three targets, GAMAF reduced aggregate mean absolute error (MAE) and root mean squared error (RMSE) by approximately 29.6% and 29.7%, respectively. Ablation analyses supported the integrated architecture, while adaptive modality weights revealed target-dependent patterns. GAMAF demonstrates the potential of generative-augmented multimodal fusion for decoding Kansei-related product impressions. However, performance comparisons remain descriptive because baseline variability and participant-level uncertainty were not quantified. Further validation on unseen product designs and closed-loop design optimization is needed to establish its generalizability and practical utility.

papers.title: Long-Term Effects of Myocardial Injury on 1-Year Outcomes in Hospital Survivors With COVID-19: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Myocardial injury is both a common complication among hospitalized coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) patients and a major predictor of adverse clinical outcomes. However, its long-term effects remain poorly defined. In this prospective cohort study of 2185 COVID-19 survivors (531 with myocardial injury), we assessed 1-year post-discharge outcomes using Kaplan-Meier analysis and multivariable Cox regression before and after propensity score matching. Myocardial injury was associated with higher all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 3.14) and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) (aHR 5.22). Long-term use of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors/angiotensin II receptor blockers (ACEI/ARB) was associated with reduced mortality (aHR 0.44) and MACE (aHR 0.58) in the myocardial injury group. At 1 year, 71.5% of survivors reported persistent symptoms-most commonly fatigue and sleep difficulties-and those with myocardial injury had poorer quality of life. This study provides the prospective evidence from China's Omicron era on the prognostic value of myocardial injury, combining hard clinical endpoints with patient-reported outcomes and the first analysis of the ACEI/ARB association in this population. These findings highlight the prognostic importance of myocardial injury and the potential role of ACEI/ARB therapy in post-discharge management, supporting targeted follow-up strategies for this high-risk population.

papers.title: Rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder as a model of early neurodegeneration: challenges for research and clinical diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) has evolved from a descriptive parasomnia to a clinically informative model for studying early neurodegenerative processes, particularly within the spectrum of α-synucleinopathies. Defined by the loss of REM sleep atonia and the emergence of dream enactment behaviors, RBD reflects dysfunction of brainstem circuits that normally suppress motor output during dreaming. Longitudinal evidence indicates that many individuals with isolated RBD eventually develop neurodegenerative disease, most commonly Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, or, less frequently, multiple system atrophy, positioning RBD among the most specific clinical markers of prodromal synucleinopathy currently recognized. Mechanistic studies suggest that RBD arises from instability within distributed REM sleep regulatory networks involving dopaminergic, noradrenergic, serotonergic, and cholinergic systems. This network dysfunction may precede classic motor and cognitive symptoms and can be accompanied by early abnormalities in neurophysiology, imaging, cognition, olfaction, autonomic function, and molecular biomarkers. These findings support a model in which RBD may represent one of the earliest clinically accessible manifestations of a multisystem neurodegenerative process, although anatomical origin, propagation patterns, and phenoconversion trajectories vary across patients. Despite these advances, clinical management remains largely symptomatic, and key challenges persist in diagnosis, risk stratification, prognostic counselling, and therapeutic development. A broader clinical framework is therefore needed, in which RBD is not viewed solely as an isolated sleep disorder but also as a potential marker of early neurodegeneration in appropriately characterized patients. Integrating polysomnography with multimodal biomarkers and network-based models of disease may refine risk stratification and support the development of targeted interventions at earlier stages of neurodegenerative disease.

papers.title: Prevalence of masked obesity and its association with body composition and lifestyle factors in young adults: a cross-sectional analysis.
papers.abstract: This study aims to investigate the prevalence of masked obesity among vocational college students, evaluate the predictive efficacy of the muscle-to-fat ratio (MFR), and explore the associations between masked obesity and lifestyle factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 320 students from Fujian Health College. A self-developed structured questionnaire was used to collect data on demographic characteristics and health-related behaviors. Body composition indicators were measured via a bioelectrical impedance analysis (InBody 770c). According to different combinations of body mass index (BMI) and body fat percentage (BF%), they were divided into the following 8 groups: (1) under weight with low body fat group (UW-L); (2) Under weight with high body fat group (UW-H); (3) Normal weight with low body fat group (NW-L); (4) Normal weight with high body fat group (NW-H); (5) Overweight with low body fat group (OW-L); (6) Overweight with high body fat group (OW-H); (7) Obese with low body fat group (OB-L); (8) Obese with high body fat group (OB-H). Among them, the two types of UW-H and NW-H together constitute masked obesity. The prevalence of masked obesity was as high as 33.9% in the normal-weight population, and 5.8% in the underweight population. MFR demonstrates better diagnostic efficacy in the detection of masked obesity (AUC = 0.861), and is superior to BMI. After adjusting for confounding factors, excessive sleep duration was associated with masked obesity (OR = 6.887, 95% CI: 1.417-33.473), while no significant association was found between sleep quality and physical activity and masked obesity. Compared with the traditional obesity index BMI, MFR is more effective in identifying masked obesity in young adults.

papers.title: Effect of Intravenous Acetaminophen on Preemptive Multimodal Analgesia for Pediatric Osteotomy Correction Surgery: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Children undergoing Osteotomy correction surgery can experience substantial postoperative pain and frequently require opioids. We evaluated whether a single preincision dose of intravenous acetaminophen, added to a standardized multimodal analgesic regimen, reduces postoperative pain and perioperative opioid requirements. In this prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 96 children aged 6-18 years undergoing elective lower-limb osteotomy correction surgery were randomized 1:1 to intravenous acetaminophen 15 mg/kg or volume-matched 0.9% sodium chloride administered 30 minutes before skin incision. The primary outcome was the incidence of moderate-to-severe pain within 72 hours after surgery, defined as a Face, Legs, Activity, Cry, Consolability (FLACC) score ≥4 at any scheduled assessment. The primary analysis used the modified intention-to-treat (mITT) population (n=95; 48 acetaminophen, 47 placebo). Secondary outcomes included perioperative opioid consumption, pain intensity, rescue analgesia, patient-controlled intravenous analgesia use, subjective sleep quality, and adverse events. The trial was prospectively registered (ChiCTR2500095363; January 6, 2025). Moderate-to-severe pain occurred in 8/48 (16.7%) versus 21/47 (44.7%) children, an absolute risk reduction of 28.0% (RR, 0.37; 95% CI, 0.2-0.8; P=0.004). Intraoperative remifentanil consumption was lower in the acetaminophen group (median, 0.8 vs 1.3 mg; between-group difference, 0.6 mg; 95% CI, 0.3-0.9; P<0.001). Postoperative 72-hour morphine-equivalent consumption was also lower (median, 90.0 vs 105.0 mg; difference, 14.4 mg; 95% CI, 2.7-26.5; P=0.018). Longitudinal ordinal GEE demonstrated significant group-by-time interactions for FLACC scores both at rest (P<0.001) and during movement (P=0.002), with the analgesic benefit concentrated in the early postoperative period. Subjective sleep NRS scores were lower in the acetaminophen group on POD1 (Holm-adjusted P=0.005), although the overall group-by-time interaction was not significant (P=0.411). No increase in perioperative adverse events was observed in the acetaminophen group. Preincision intravenous acetaminophen was associated with a lower incidence of moderate-to-severe postoperative pain and reduced opioid requirements in children undergoing osteotomy correction surgery. Larger multicenter trials are warranted to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Association between Some Demographic and Fertility-related Characteristics and Sleep Quality among Women with Infertility: A Cross-sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Infertility is associated with a considerable psychological and social burden that can negatively impact women's quality of life and sleep quality. The current study aimed to examine the association of sleep quality with some demographic and fertility-related characteristics among women with infertility. A cross-sectional study was carried out in the fertility clinic of AL Kadhomiya Teaching Hospital from January to December 2024 in Baghdad, Iraq. In total, 273 women with infertility aged 20-49 years were recruited. Participants' sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index. Data analysis was done using descriptive statistics, chi-square test, and a binary logistic regression model through SPSS version 25. At least 193 participants (70.70%) said they slept poorly. In binary logistic regression analysis, age and sleep duration were predictors of poor sleep quality. Women aged 40-49 years had significantly higher odds of poor sleep quality compared with women 20-29 years old (OR=2.53, 95% CI: 1.13-5.67, P=0.024). Women who slept 6-7 hours per night had reduced risks of poor sleep quality compared to those who slept less than 4 hours (OR=0.24, 95% CI: 0.13-0.46, P<0.001). Poor sleep quality was not associated with body mass index and the duration of trying to conceive (P>0.05). Poor sleep was common among women with infertility. Older age and shorter sleep duration were found to be associated with poor sleep quality. Attention to these variables may help identify women with infertility at risk for sleep quality disturbances and design a program to manage their problem.
papers.journal: International journal of community based nursing and midwifery

papers.title: Associations between Mediterranean lifestyle and its components with cardiovascular outcomes among community-dwelling older adults.
papers.abstract: The present study examined the cross-sectional and longitudinal associations of adherence to the Mediterranean lifestyle (MEDLS) and its individual components with cardiovascular outcomes among older adults in England. Data from 565 adults aged ≥65 years participating in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing were analyzed. MEDLS adherence (score range: 0-24) comprised six domains: Mediterranean diet adherence, physical activity, water intake, sleep, social isolation, and cooking activities. The outcomes of interest were hypertension, heart attack (myocardial infarction/coronary thrombosis), and stroke. Logistic regression models were used to examine cross-sectional and longitudinal associations, with analyses adjusted for age and sex. Among 565 participants, 96 had hypertension, 14 had experienced a heart attack, and 10 had experienced a stroke at baseline; 42, 16, and 13 incident cases, respectively, were identified during follow-up. Higher MEDLS adherence was cross-sectionally associated with lower odds of hypertension (OR 0.849, 95% CI 0.722-0.999). No statistically significant longitudinal associations were observed between MEDLS and hypertension (OR 0.990, 95% CI 0.902-1.085), heart attack (OR 0.919, 95% CI 0.707-1.195), or stroke (OR 1.053, 95% CI 0.827-1.341), although the small number of events limited precision. At the component level, Mediterranean diet adherence was associated with lower odds of incident heart attack (OR 0.670, 95% CI 0.454-0.988); However, this finding was considered exploratory. Higher adherence to the MEDLS was associated with lower odds of prevalent hypertension but not with incident cardiovascular outcomes among communitydwelling older adults. At the component level, greater adherence to the Mediterranean diet was prospectively associated with lower odds of heart attack; however, given the absence of adjustment for multiple comparisons, this finding should be considered exploratory and requires confirmation in adequately powered studies.

papers.title: Poststroke sleep phenotypes and executive dysfunction: toward a sleep-network-executive framework.
papers.abstract: Post-stroke sleep disturbance and executive dysfunction frequently coexist, yet the mechanisms linking disturbed sleep to cognitive recovery remain poorly understood. A major challenge is phenotypic heterogeneity: insomnia, sleep fragmentation, obstructive sleep apnea, hypersomnolence, and circadian disruption differ in their biological drivers and cognitive consequences. To develop a testable network-level account, we conducted a targeted synthesis of clinical stroke studies, stroke neuroimaging research, non-stroke sleep-network evidence, and intervention studies, mapping each evidence stream according to its proximity to the proposed pathway. The synthesis indicates that focal lesions, diaschisis, and structural disconnection after stroke can disrupt the integrity and coordination of the salience, default mode, and frontoparietal networks. Clinical studies support an association between disturbed sleep and poorer post-stroke cognition, while neuroimaging findings demonstrate altered large scale network organization in post-stroke cognitive impairment. Evidence from non-stroke populations further suggests that sleep loss, insomnia, and sleep fragmentation can impair network segregation, default mode regulation, frontoparietal recruitment, and salience-network-mediated switching. We therefore propose that sleep fragmentation, insomnia, and arousal instability may act as functional stressors on an already vulnerable post-stroke network architecture. Inefficient switching may permit context-inappropriate persistence of default mode activity and reduce or delay frontoparietal engagement during executive demand, thereby contributing to impaired conflict monitoring, working memory, processing speed, and cognitive flexibility. No study has directly tested this complete pathway within a single stroke cohort. The framework should therefore be regarded as a falsifiable mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal model. Future studies should combine objective sleep phenotyping, dynamic and effective connectivity, task based neuroimaging, domain specific executive measures, and longitudinal or interventional designs within the same stroke cohorts.

papers.title: Language usage shapes neural mechanisms of code-switching.
papers.abstract: Linguistic environments play an important role in shaping the mechanisms of language processing. The current study examined how neural responses to bilingual code-switching vary as a function of ongoing language usage, and which control processes may underlie these differences. Forty highly proficient English-French bilinguals listened to continuous spoken narratives containing inter-sentential switches. Participants were matched for proficiency and language background but differed in their current L2 usage (Active vs. Inactive). Narratives alternated either between their first and second languages, or between language and an acoustically matched non-linguistic signal, providing a means to probe language disengagement and re-engagement. While comprehension and cortical speech tracking were comparable across groups, oscillatory analyses revealed a usage-dependent modulation of alpha-band activity. Active bilinguals showed comparable alpha responses to switch and non-switch sentences, whereas Inactive bilinguals showed reduced alpha power following language switches, emerging from 650 ms over parieto-occipital regions. The direction, timing, and location of this effect are consistent with later attention control processes rather than early perceptual responses to the switch. Further analyses suggested that group differences were more closely associated with language disengagement than re-engagement. Together, these findings demonstrate an association between current L2 usage and alpha-band responses during language switching, suggesting that ongoing language experience may be modulating the neural mechanisms of language control.

papers.title: Development and expert appraisal of a lifestyle questionnaire for microbiome host metadata.
papers.abstract: Lifestyle information can help contextualize variation in the human gut microbiome, but its collection and operational definitions differ across studies. We developed a candidate questionnaire combining diet, physical activity and sleep for microbiome host metadata and undertook an initial appraisal by Italian experts. Candidate content was informed by a focused narrative literature appraisal and established lifestyle-assessment frameworks. Seventeen experts were invited and nine responded (53%). In a single anonymous rating round, experts assessed the relevance of 37 candidate items on a five-point scale. The prespecified agreement criterion was at least 70% of respondents assigning a rating of 4 or 5, corresponding to at least seven of nine experts. Twenty-five items (67.6%) met this criterion: 18 of 23 dietary items (78.3%), six of eight physicalactivity items (75.0%), and one of six sleep items (16.7%). Twelve items remained exploratory. These findings provide an initial prioritization of candidate lifestyle metadata within an Italian specialist network. They do not establish a stable iterative Delphi consensus, instrument reliability, construct validity, or associations between questionnaire responses and microbiome outcomes. Participant testing, operational refinement and empirical evaluation are required before research deployment or potential use in fecal microbiota transplantation donor characterization.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

papers.title: The influencing factors of postoperative sleep disturbance in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery and the construction and validation of a machine learning prediction model.
papers.abstract: Postoperative sleep disturbance (POSD) is a common complication in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery, which impairs recovery and increases disease burden. To date, prediction models for POSD in this population, particularly those based on machine learning techniques, remain scarce. To investigate the incidence and influencing factors of POSD in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery, and to construct prediction models based on conventional logistic regression and seven machine learning algorithms. A total of 563 elderly patients who underwent elective transurethral prostate surgery at our hospital between March 2024 and December 2025 were prospectively enrolled and randomly divided into a training set (n = 338) and a validation set (n = 225) at a ratio of 6:4. LASSO regression (with lambda.1se) was used to screen predictive variables, and multivariate logistic regression to identify independent risk factors. Logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), naive Bayes, decision tree, support vector machine, k-nearest neighbors, and artificial neural network models were constructed. Model performance was evaluated using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed for interpretability analysis of the optimal model. The incidence of POSD was 62.2%. Independent risk factors included preoperative anxiety (Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Anxiety [HADS-A] score), nocturia frequency (≥3 times/night), elevated systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), preoperative noise score, and moderate-to-severe cough-related pain (P < 0.05). The random forest model demonstrated the best overall performance, with an AUC of 0.926 (95% CI: 0.89-0.96) in the training set and 0.964 (95% CI: 0.93-0.99) in the validation set, and exhibited superior calibration and clinical utility compared with the other models. SHAP analysis revealed that the HADS-A score contributed the most to the predictions. Preoperative anxiety, increased nocturia frequency (≥3 times/night), elevated SII, high noise score, and moderate-to-severe cough-related pain are independent risk factors for POSD in elderly patients undergoing transurethral prostate surgery. The random forest prediction model exhibits optimal performance and can be used for early clinical risk identification and individualized intervention. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR2600124377.

papers.title: Studying multiple health behaviours in older adults using a measurement burst design: protocol, feasibility, compliance, behavioural patterns and lessons learned.
papers.abstract: Overweight and obesity are major public health challenges, requiring preventive efforts targeting diet, physical activity (PA), sedentary behaviour (SB) and sleep. Current research often treats these behaviours in isolation, ignores daily fluctuations and focuses on between-person differences. Studies examining the temporal covariance of these behaviours, assessing within-day and day-to-day variations in determinants and exploring how these time-varying determinants predict within-person variability in behaviours are needed. This paper aims to evaluate the feasibility of a measurement burst design with repeated intensive longitudinal assessments and to present patterns of behaviours and determinants. A 12-month observational study with a measurement burst design was conducted (January-December 2025). In total, 130 participants aged 55-75 years enrolled in the study, which consisted of four 7-day measurement bursts. Data collection included monitoring of diet, PA, SB, sleep and time-based ecological momentary assessment (EMA). Compliance rates, descriptive statistics per burst and across bursts were computed. 116 participants completed all bursts (retention rate = 89·2 %). Compliance rates ranged from 83·5 % for time-based EMA to 91·8 % for SB, supporting feasibility of the protocol. Mean values of 1692 kcal/day (sd = 565) for energy intake, 9·4 h/day (sd = 2·4) for sedentary time and 10 610 steps/day (sd = 6302) were observed. Mean daily light, moderate and vigorous PA-levels were 102·9 (sd = 37·4), 65·5 (sd = 43·4) and 11·5 (sd = 17·0) minutes, respectively. Mean sleep duration was 6·4 h/night (sd = 1·3), with a mean sleep efficiency of 79·2 % (sd = 10·2). This paper demonstrated the feasibility of integrating multiple assessment methods within a measurement burst design for studying health behaviours in adults aged 55-75 years and highlighted the value of analyses at more fine-grained temporal and individual levels.

papers.title: Skin Seed Amplification Assay Differentiates Multiple System Atrophy from Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Misdiagnoses of multiple system atrophy (MSA) and Parkinson's disease (PD) remain common. The objective of the study was to develop a skin α-synuclein seed amplification assay (αSyn-SAA) for detecting pathological α-synuclein and distinguishing MSA from PD. In this blinded, cross-sectional study, 308 skin biopsies from 117 participants were analyzed using a standardized thioflavin T fluorescence-based αSyn-SAA protocol. The cohort included 42 PD, 31 MSA, 30 controls, and 14 progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP) cases. Kinetic parameters were analyzed to differentiate PD from MSA, and matched skin cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) analyses were performed. Assay thresholds were predefined using brain lysates from neuropathologically confirmed cases. Fibril morphology from amplified skin samples was compared to postmortem brain using proteinase K digestion and electron microscopy. αSyn-SAA detected synucleinopathy (PD or MSA) with 82.2% sensitivity and 90% specificity versus controls. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis showed that maximum fluorescence (Fmax, area under the curve [AUC] = 0.93) and lag time (AUC = 0.91) distinguished PD from MSA at the biopsy level. SAA positivity correlated with rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) in both disorders. Among SAA-positive cases, the 50% mean Fmax cutoff correctly classified the underlying synucleinopathy in 81.7% of cases (49 of 60). Disease-specific kinetic and structural signatures were reproducible across laboratories and αSyn substrate batches and were supported by concordant findings in a subset of skin samples matched to CSF, MRI data, and postmortem brain tissue. Skin αSyn-SAA detects pathological α-synuclein in living patients with high accuracy and distinguishes MSA from PD based on assay kinetics and fibril strain properties, supporting its potential as a biomarker to distinguish among synucleinopathies. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.
papers.journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society

papers.title: Temporal Associations Between Physiological Sleep and Next-Day Pain Intensity in Individuals With Activity-Limiting Chronic Pain: A Multiple Night At-Home Ear-EEG Sleep-Monitoring Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain and sleep disturbances frequently co-occur. However, most prior research relies on self-report or actigraphy, which reflect behavioural aspects of sleep but provide only limited insight into the underlying sleep physiology. In this pre-registered prospective observational study (NCT06368531), we investigated within-person night-to-night variability in physiological sleep metrics and explored temporal associations between sleep metrics and next-day pain. Individuals with bothersome (n = 4) or high-impact (n = 15) chronic pain completed between 11 and 33 nights of at-home sleep monitoring using an ear-EEG device and rated morning pain intensity daily on a 0-10 numerical rating scale. This design enables assessment of real-world physiological sleep patterns alongside natural fluctuations in pain, offering a high-resolution view of sleep-pain dynamics beyond traditional diary or actigraphy-based methods. Substantial between-night variability was observed across multiple sleep metrics, such as sleep efficiency and sleep stage transitions (ICC values < 0.5), indicating that less than half of the total variance was attributable to differences between subjects, underscoring the importance of longitudinal within-person monitoring. Mixed-effects model analyses revealed that lower next-day pain intensity was associated with greater duration (β = -0.01, p = 0.005), higher percentage (β = -0.07, p = 0.001) and increased stability (β = -0.01, p = 0.013) of N3 sleep. In contrast, higher next-day pain was associated with increased N3 fragmentation (β = 0.01, p = 0.014) and a higher proportion of N1 sleep (β = 0.014, p = 0.007). Together, these findings provide objective physiological support for previously reported associations between sleep and pain, highlighting the value of longitudinal ear-EEG monitoring for capturing nightly sleep-pain dynamics. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06368531.

papers.title: Photoperiodic Regulation of SK Channels in Dorsal Raphe Serotonin Neurons.
papers.abstract: Day length, or seasonal photoperiod, shapes mood and affective behaviors, but the neural mechanisms underlying these effects are still being defined. Serotonin neurons of the dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) are critical regulators of affective behaviors, and photoperiod modulates their excitability and ongoing activity. Here, we investigated the influence of seasonal photoperiod on the function and expression of small conductance calcium-activated potassium (SK) channels, which mediate the after-hyperpolarizing potential (AHP) in dorsal raphe serotonin neurons. Building on previous work demonstrating that long summer-like photoperiod increases serotonergic neuron excitability and decreases AHP amplitude, we hypothesized that day length influences SK channel activity, thereby contributing to differences in neuronal excitability observed between Long, Equinox, and Short photoperiod conditions. Using multielectrode array recordings from DRN slices, we found a significant, dose-dependent increase in spike rate upon application of the SK channel inhibitor apamin, indicating that SK channels indeed influence the spike rate of dorsal raphe serotonin neurons. In addition, whole-cell recordings from DRN neurons in slices demonstrated that SK channel-mediated AHP currents were smaller in amplitude in Long photoperiod mice compared to Short and Equinox photoperiod mice. However, we found no significant differences in mRNA levels of the SK3 subunit (Kcnn3) in DRN serotonin neurons across photoperiod conditions as determined by single-molecule fluorescence in situ hybridization. Overall, these findings indicate that photoperiod modulates SK channel function in DRN serotonin neurons, possibly through posttranscriptional mechanisms, contributing to the increase in serotonin neuron excitability observed in long summer-like photoperiods.

papers.title: Trans-septal suturing versus intranasal splinting following septoplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: To compare the efficacy and safety of trans-septal suturing versus intranasal splinting after septoplasty through a systematic review and meta-analysis, focusing on post-operative complications and patient-centred outcomes. Comparative studies directly evaluating both techniques were included. Pooled odds ratios and standardised mean differences with 95 per cent confidence intervals were calculated. Seventeen studies involving 1502 patients were included. No significant differences were found in adhesion, crust formation, septal haematoma, septal perforation or post-operative bleeding. Trans-septal suturing significantly reduced post-operative pain (standardised mean differences, -1.09; 95 per cent confidence intervals, -1.68 to -0.49) and sleep disturbance (standardised mean differences, -0.32; 95 per cent confidence intervals, -0.60 to -0.05) but increased operative time (standardised mean differences, 0.65; 95 per cent confidence intervals, 0.19-1.10). Infection and epiphora tended to be less frequent with trans-septal suturing. Both techniques provide comparable protection against major post-operative complications, but trans-septal suturing improves post-operative comfort at the cost of a modest increase in operative time.
papers.journal: The Journal of laryngology and otology

papers.title: Physiological Sleep Features Associated With Dimensions of Daily Dysfunction in Insomnia.
papers.abstract: Daily dysfunction is a key criterion of insomnia, but its underlying structure and relationship with objective sleep physiology remain unclear. This study aimed to identify the dimensions of subjective daily dysfunction using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) in individuals with insomnia and to examine its association with polysomnography (PSG) macroarchitecture, electroencephalographic (EEG) spectral power and odds ratio product (ORP)-based sleep depth in individuals with and without insomnia. We hypothesized that more severe daily dysfunction would be associated with poorer sleep continuity, higher high-frequency EEG activity and lighter sleep depth. The final sample included 859 adults (50.1% female; mean age 44.2 ± 14.1 years) in the Sleep Apnea Global Interdisciplinary Consortium (SAGIC) without obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) or shift work, including 368 with insomnia. EFA supported a single factor underlying the nine daily dysfunction items, which were combined into a total score. In univariate linear regression analyses adjusted for age, sex and site, higher beta-1 power and several ORP measures were nominally associated with more severe daily dysfunction, but none of them survived correction for multiple comparisons. No significant predictor-by-group interactions were observed. Across three levels of sleep physiology-PSG macroarchitecture, spectral power, and continuous sleep depth-no sleep measure was associated with daily dysfunction after correction for multiple comparisons. PSG macroarchitecture and sleep EEG-derived measures may not fully capture daily dysfunction. Future studies could examine whether within-night sleep dynamics are more informative than whole-night averages.

papers.title: Impairment of ictal consciousness and psychosis in drug-resistant focal epilepsy: A retrospective clinical cohort study.
papers.abstract: Psychoses of epilepsy (POE) affect up to 13% of patients with focal epilepsy. Whereas interictal risk factors are well documented, ictal correlates of POE remain poorly characterized. We hypothesized that an impairment of ictal consciousness on the Consciousness Seizure Scale (CSS), would be associated with POE. We assessed the association between ictal clinical features and POE compared to non-POE in adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. We retrospectively analyzed a presurgical cohort of adults with drug-resistant focal epilepsy monitored by video-electroencephalography (EEG) or stereo-EEG. For each patient, all seizures with an examination allowing the completion of CSS score were included. POE were identified through standardized psychiatric interviews. Association between ictal features, primarily CSS score, and POE was tested using generalized estimating equations (GEE). Among 232 included seizures (25 from POE group, 207 from non-POE group), the probability of POE varied nonlinearly with ictal consciousness; it peaked at intermediate CSS scores (GEE, OR = 4.31, p = .006). This effect remained after adjustment for duration of both epilepsy (OR=1.06, p = .005) and seizure (OR=1.20, p = .013). Intraclass correlation of CSS was .76 (95%CI, .65-.85), reflecting a low within-patient variance. An older age, more severe depressive and anxiety symptoms were also associated with POE. POE were associated with intermediate impairment of ictal consciousness, suggesting that partial disruption of awareness may favor the emergence of psychotic symptoms. The high level of intrapatient stability for CSS, mostly estimated from non-POE, suggests that CSS could be constant across seizures. This raises the possibility that POE risk could stem from the way consciousness is altered during seizures.

papers.title: Glial Control of Insomnia: Astrocyte-Microglia Interactions in Stress, Hyperarousal and Sleep Dysregulation.
papers.abstract: Insomnia is a highly prevalent and burdensome sleep disorder whose pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. While traditional models have emphasized neuronal hyperarousal, accumulating evidence indicates that glial cells-particularly astrocytes and microglia-play central and complementary roles in the regulation of sleep-wake dynamics and the persistence of chronic insomnia. This review synthesizes clinical, experimental and translational evidence supporting a dual regulatory framework in which astrocytes and microglia act as key integrators of stress signalling, neuroinflammation, synaptic plasticity and sleep homeostasis. Astrocytes emerge as primary modulators of metabolic and neuro-modulatory coupling within sleep-wake circuits, linking hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis activation to dysregulated adenosine signalling, excitatory-inhibitory imbalance, impaired glymphatic clearance and circadian misalignment. In parallel, microglia function as immune and synaptic sculptors, with chronic sleep disturbance biasing them toward maladaptive activation states characterized by altered cytokine release, disrupted synaptic pruning and stress hormone-dependent signalling cascades. Although direct glia-resolved evidence in human insomnia remains limited, convergent findings from neuroimaging, animal models and sleep-immune research support a coordinated stress-glia-insomnia axis. We further highlight mechanisms of astrocyte-microglia crosstalk, including purinergic signalling, inflammatory feedback loops and calcium-dependent network synchronization, which may stabilize pathological hyperarousal states. Finally, we discuss emerging glia-targeted therapeutic strategies and key translational challenges, emphasizing the need for cell-type-specific biomarkers, spatiotemporally precise interventions and personalized treatment frameworks.

papers.title: Implementation of the seizure code in a tertiary hospital: Effects on emergency care times and clinical outcomes in severe seizures.
papers.abstract: To assess the impact of implementing the Seizure Code (SC), a structured multidisciplinary emergency protocol for severe seizures, on care times and clinical outcomes at a tertiary hospital. Single-center, retrospective observational study including episodes of severe seizures in patients aged 18 years or older managed between January 2023 and December 2024, comparing pre-SC and post-SC periods. The primary outcome was time from seizure onset to administration of the first anti-seizure medication (ASM). Secondary outcomes included other care intervals, process indicators, and clinical outcomes. Care intervals were analyzed with accelerated failure time models (percentage change in median time), length of stay in a competing-risks framework, and binary outcomes with Firth-penalized logistic regression (odds ratios, OR), all adjusted for prespecified covariates and clustered by patient. Of 1959 episodes identified, 378 (175 pre-SC, 203 post-SC) met SC activation criteria. Time to the first ASM, the primary outcome, did not differ significantly (27% shorter, 95% CI -15% to 53% for benzodiazepines; 27%, -6% to 50% for others). Time to urgent video-EEG (VEEG) was 48% shorter (29%-61%) and the neurological assessment-VEEG interval 63% shorter (31%-80%). Pre-notification by Emergency Medical Services increased (22.9% vs. 37.8%; p = 0.003). Hospital stay (7.48 vs. 5.08 days; subdistribution hazard ratio for discharge alive 1.36, 1.02-1.89) and intensive care unit stay (3.20 vs. 1.48 days) were shorter. Thirty-day seizure recurrence was lower (8.0% vs. 3.0%; adjusted OR 0.33, 0.12-0.84). Mortality and functional status at discharge did not differ. The primary outcome, time to first anti-seizure medication, was not significantly shorter after implementation of the structured emergency protocol. The observed benefits were concentrated in secondary process and resource-utilization indicators: implementation of the Seizure Code was associated with faster access to urgent VEEG, shorter hospital and intensive care unit stays, and lower 30-day seizure recurrence, without a significant effect on mortality. These findings support protocolized emergency pathways in severe seizures. Severe seizures are emergencies in which fast, coordinated care matters. We compared how patients were treated at one hospital before and after a new protocol, the Seizure Code, was introduced. Afterwards, patients had urgent video-EEG (a recording of brain activity) sooner and spent fewer days in hospital and in the intensive care unit, and fewer had another seizure within 30 days. However, the time to the first anti-seizure medication did not change significantly, and deaths and disability at discharge were unchanged.

papers.title: Preferential Improvement of Trauma-Related Distressing Dreams Following Traumatic Memory Reactivation in Severe PTSD: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Trauma-related distressing dreams are among the most frequent and persistent symptoms of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Propranolol has been proposed to modulate the reconsolidation of reactivated emotional memories through beta-adrenergic blockade, providing a rationale for its combination with traumatic memory reactivation procedures (TMRP). In this exploratory post hoc secondary analysis of the REDUCTRAUMA2 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial, we examined changes in distressing dreams severity during and after TMRP administered under propranolol or placebo in 66 patients with PTSD. Distressing dreams were assessed using item 2 of the PTSD Checklist-Specific (PCL-S). Distressing dreams severity decreased markedly following the intervention in the whole cohort, with large within-subject effects maintained up to 3 months. No significant differences were observed between propranolol and placebo. In the overall cohort, distressing dreams improved preferentially compared with the remaining PTSD symptoms at one-week and one-month follow-up. Subgroup analyses showed that this preferential improvement was sustained across all follow-up assessments in participants with severe PTSD at baseline, whereas no preferential effect was observed in the non-severe subgroup. Distribution-free RIDIT analyses yielded convergent findings. These exploratory findings suggest that trauma-related distressing dreams may represent a particularly treatment-responsive symptom dimension in PTSD, especially among patients with more severe symptomatology. No additional benefit of propranolol over placebo was observed; however, in the absence of a non-reactivation control condition, the specific contribution of TMRP to the observed improvement cannot be determined. Prospective studies using dedicated nightmare measures and appropriate control conditions are needed to confirm these findings. Trail Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01713556.

papers.title: [Phytotherapy in the management of insomnia and depressive disorders].
papers.abstract: Insomnia and depression are common conditions encountered in general practice, for which first-line treatments may be associated with notable adverse effects. Several medicinal plants may offer complementary therapeutic options. The oral administration of valerian root extract may contribute to a subjective improvement in sleep quality, as may the inhalation of lavender essential oil. St. John's wort represents a relevant therapeutic option for the management of depressive symptoms, with efficacy comparable to that of selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors, and better tolerability. However, its use should be avoided in individuals receiving medications metabolized by hepatic enzymes or in women using oral contraceptives.

papers.title: Integrating uncertainty and practice variability for epilepsy prognostication after intracranial EEG: A meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Intracranial electroencephalography (iEEG) practices and diagnostic testing vary among institutions, limiting standardization and optimization of surgical outcomes. This study estimates resection rates and surgical outcome effect sizes after iEEG and develops individual patient-level data (IPD) models using the missing-indicator method to approximate real-world clinical uncertainties and practice variability in iEEG and surgical decision-making. Databases were queried for studies reporting ≥12-month outcomes after epilepsy surgery in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) who underwent iEEG. Random-effects meta-analysis estimated pooled outcome proportions. IPD analysis was performed using multivariable generalized linear regression and logistic regression models with cross-validation and calibration assessment. Missing values for key predictors were retained as a "not specified" category to evaluate the impact of incorporating uncertainty in common clinical data on outcome prediction. Primary outcomes were seizure freedom (Engel class IA or International League Against Epilepsy [ILAE] 1) and favorable seizure outcomes (Engel I or ILAE 1-2). Of 4975 studies identified, 115 met the inclusion criteria. The pooled frequency of patients undergoing resection after iEEG was 67% (95% confidence interval [CI] 60%-74%), 52% achieved seizure freedom (95% CI 48%-56%), and 58% achieved a favorable outcome (95% CI 54%-62%). IPD analysis included 1305 patients from 29 studies and identified a lesional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; odds ratio [OR] 1.94, CI 1.48-2.55, p < .0001) and a cortical malformation (OR 1.47, CI 1.08-2.00, p = .01) as independent predictors of a favorable outcome, whereas iEEG implantation strategy (bilateral implantation OR .61, 95% CI .42-.89, p = .01) was an independent predictor of a less favorable outcome. About two-thirds of patients undergoing iEEG proceeded to resection, and about half achieved seizure freedom. Multivariable models incorporating clinical uncertainty and practice variability were well calibrated. However, modest discrimination suggests that routinely available clinical variables alone have limited ability to predict individual surgical outcomes. More standardized and granular clinical and practice-related data may improve individualized prognostication after iEEG.

papers.title: A systemic auxin state integrates light and temperature to gate lateral rooting in Arabidopsis.
papers.abstract: How plants coordinate local organ formation with systemic information about environmental conditions remains largely unclear. Here we show that availability of the phytohormone auxin across the Arabidopsis root provides a shared hormonal state that integrates environmental cues and gates whether locally specified branching sites develop. Long-term luminescence imaging, time-resolved transcriptomics and metabolite profiling reveal approximately 24-hour rhythms in auxin abundance and signalling at 21°C, with shoot-perceived light setting the amplitude of the systemic signalling. At 29°C, this organisation is reprogrammed into a root-wide decline followed by a light-dependent systemic recovery of auxin signalling. Recovery under sufficient light supports root branching-site progression without requiring restored circadian rhythmicity. In contrast, weaker recovery under reduced light leads to arrest of early primordia. Genetic analyses implicate phytochrome B as well as cryptochromes photoreceptors and the morning loop of the circadian clock in this conditional response. The auxin oxidase DIOXYGENASE FOR AUXIN OXIDATION 1 (DAO1) reprograms systemic auxin dynamics at elevated temperature. Reducing auxin oxidation sustains signalling in branching sites and lateral root development during warming, whereas increased oxidation weakens recovery and enhances developmental inhibition. Our findings reveal how systemic metabolic control allows plants to interpret global environmental information in context and therewith align local de novo organ formation.

papers.title: The Role of Shift Work Schedule in Shaping Eating Behaviors Among Nurses.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND Lifestyle factors, including dietary habits, play a crucial role in shaping health outcomes. For 2-shift workers, disruptions in circadian rhythm may further influence eating behaviors. This study aimed to assess the diet quality and selected nutritional behaviors of nurses working in different shift systems. MATERIAL AND METHODS The study included 236 nurses, with data collected using the standardized KomPAN questionnaire. Participants' height and weight were measured according to standard procedures. Nurses working in either a single-shift system (fixed working hours, no rotation) or a 2-shift system were included. Participants had a minimum of 6 months' experience in their system and consented to participate in the study. RESULTS Overall diet quality was neutral, with low intensity of pro-healthy and unhealthy dietary behaviors; low Pro-Healthy Diet Index and low Non-Healthy Diet Index co-occurred most frequently (OR=39; P<0.0001). Two-shift workers consumed more salty snacks (27% vs 12%; P=0.009) and full-fat milk (P=0.034), whereas single-shift workers more frequently chose reduced-fat milk and stewed meat dishes (P=0.012). Age was associated with dietary patterns, with younger nurses consuming more fast food, sweetened drinks, and alcohol. No significant relationships were found between the single-shift/2-shift systems and BMI, overall diet indices, or meal regularity. These findings highlight the subtle dietary differences associated with different shift systems. CONCLUSIONS The overall diet quality among nurses was low, regardless of work schedule. Although general diet indices did not differ by shift system, specific behaviors reflected the association between work schedule and food choices. Workplace-based nutritional interventions promoting healthy eating are recommended, particularly for 2-shift working nurses.
papers.journal: Medical science monitor : international medical journal of experimental and clinical research

papers.title: Single-Step Electrochemical Aptasensor for Melatonin Detection in Unprocessed Plasma.
papers.abstract: Melatonin is a clinically relevant biomarker for diagnosing circadian rhythm sleep disorders (CRSDs) and monitoring circadian disruption associated with cancer, metabolic and cardiovascular disease, and psychiatric disorders. This work reports the implementation of an electrochemical aptamer-based biosensor (E-aptasensor) for direct reagentless detection of melatonin within physiological levels. The E-aptasensor employs an optimized surface population of the aptamers in a conformational change-based assay to detect melatonin over a broad dynamic range, including the picomolar physiological range. The behavior of the aptameric assay was validated both in bulk solution and in silico using fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) and molecular docking (MD). The E-aptasensor achieves sensitive and selective melatonin detection, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 0.75 pM and strong specificity against a panel of relevant interferents. Fitting the electrochemical responses to the Hill-Langmuir (HL) binding model yielded an apparent electrochemical dissociation constant (Kd, app) of 37 pM. Notably, the E-aptasensor showed promising performance in unextracted human plasma, avoiding the extraction step typically required for immunoassays. These features support future development of rapid melatonin profiling for CRSD diagnosis and monitoring, as well as future point-of-care implementation. The single-step E-aptasensor offers a promising, faster, and simpler complement to gold-standard techniques.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Condylar Subtyping and Its Association With Obstructive Sleep Apnea Severity in Adults: Implication for Craniofacial Skeletal Phenotype.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association between three-dimensional (3D) condylar resorption pattern and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity in adults, and to explore its structural implications within the craniofacial skeletal phenotype (CSP) framework. Condylar morphology was classified using a two-axis system integrating the degree of resorption and cortical remodelling pattern. Patients were grouped into no resorption (NR), adaptive remodelling (AR), and severe resorption (SR) categories. Dentoskeletal, temporomandibular joint (TMJ), and polysomnographic variables were compared among groups. Multivariable regression analyses were adjusted for age, sex, and body mass index, and hierarchical regression was used to examine the contribution of condylar grouping beyond CSP. Severe condylar resorption was identified in 23.9% of the sample and was more prevalent (54.0%) in patients with CSP features. The SR group demonstrated greater skeletal discrepancy and higher apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), respiratory disturbance index (RDI), and arousal index (ArI) values (all, p < 0.05). After adjustment for age, sex, and body mass index and false discovery rate correction, SR remained significantly associated with higher AHI, RDI, and ArI, whereas TMJ pain history, condylar angulation, and oxygenation-related indices showed no significant associations. In hierarchical models, the overall incremental contribution of condylar grouping beyond CSP was not significant after multiple-testing correction; however, SR remained significantly associated with higher AHI and RDI after additional adjustment for CSP (both, FDR-adjusted p = 0.045). Severe condylar resorption was associated with greater skeletal discrepancy and higher OSA burden. Three-dimensional TMJ assessment may complement conventional skeletal phenotyping in adult OSA.

papers.title: Personalized Postoperative Pain Management and Therapies Based on Pharmacogenomics.
papers.abstract: Postoperative pain management must account for differences in drug metabolism, pain phenotype, prior opioid exposure, psychosocial vulnerability, and cognitive function. This narrative review proposes a staged precision-medicine framework separating clinically actionable pharmacogenomics from heterogeneous risk modifiers and investigational adjuncts. The strongest actionable guidance concerns CYP2D6-guided codeine and tramadol prescribing. Other genetic markers require interpretation alongside procedure-specific pain, comorbidities, medication exposure, and patient preferences rather than use as deterministic prescribing rules. Dopamine-related pathways provide a mechanistic link between pain, reward, motivation, and attention. Parkinson disease illustrates dopamine-pain interactions but is not a direct model of postoperative pain. Reward Deficiency Syndrome, the Genetic Addiction Risk Severity/Score, and the Reward Deficiency Syndrome Questionnaire-29 are considered exploratory constructs rather than validated tools for postoperative prescribing. The Continuous Visual Attention Test may offer objective neurocognitive monitoring through reaction time, response variability, and error measures. These measures are not pain-specific and require interpretation in the context of anesthesia, opioids, sedatives, sleep disruption, mood, delirium, baseline cognition, and pain intensity. Prospective studies should determine whether integrating clinical assessment, established pharmacogenomic guidance, and investigational behavioral and neurocognitive measures improves pain outcomes, opioid requirements, adherence, functional recovery, and safety. The framework defines research priorities and implementation endpoints while preserving multimodal analgesia, opioid stewardship, and clinical judgment as the foundation of care.

papers.title: Patterns and Predictors of Engagement With a Mobile Mental Health Intervention Among Hurricane-Affected Adults.
papers.abstract: Mental disorders commonly increase after disasters, yet access to care is often limited by logistical barriers. Digital mental health applications may help address these gaps by providing private, low-cost, and readily accessible support. The authors examined patterns and predictors of engagement with Bounce Back Now (BBN), a self-help mobile application (app) designed to address posttraumatic stress, depression, and sleep disturbance among disaster-affected adults. Participants included 1,357 adults affected by Hurricanes Harvey, Irma, Maria, Florence, or Michael. Use data were passively collected in the BBN app. Generalized linear models were used to examine demographic and clinical predictors of number of logins to the app and frequency of module access. Of the 717 participants randomly assigned to BBN, most accessed the activate (84%) and coping tools (87%) modules. Income emerged as the only consistent demographic predictor of multiple outcomes. Lower income was significantly associated with more frequent access to the coping tools (b=-0.20, p=0.003) and activate (b=-0.03, p=0.035) modules, as well as greater odds of accessing these modules. These findings challenge assumptions about a persistent digital divide in engagement with mental health mobile apps and suggest that digital interventions designed to minimize access barriers may successfully reach economically marginalized populations after disasters. These results have important implications for the design and dissemination of scalable digital interventions to improve access to care in postdisaster contexts.

papers.title: The effect of a seven-week online mindfulness intervention on the relationship between menstrual symptoms and mental health - A non-randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Menstrual symptoms are common among physically active women and may affect their well-being and performance. Moreover, symptom frequency has been associated with mental health in previous studies. Although mindfulness-based interventions (MBI) have shown beneficial effects on psychological and physiological health outcomes, their potential role in the relationship between menstrual and mental health remains unclear. Therefore, this study examined whether participation in an MBI was associated with changes in this relationship. 39 physically active students were split into an experimental group (EG; n = 14; 22.68 ± 2.23 years) and a control group (CG; n = 25; 22.76 ± 4.88 years), which conducted a baseline and post-intervention measurement, including a psychometric screening. The CG received no intervention during the study and was offered access to the intervention materials afterwards. Assessed constructs included the 21-item version of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale and the Menstrual Symptom index (MSi). The MBI was developed based on mindfulness-based stress reduction, incorporating the dimensions of acting with awareness, non-judgmental acceptance, and present-moment attention. At baseline in the control group, MSi scores were positively associated with anxiety (B = 0.16; p = .004) and depression (B = 0.14; p = .012). No significant group × time interactions were observed for depression or stress. For anxiety, the group × time interaction was significant at the grand-mean MSi score (B = - 3.30; 95% CI [- 6.50, - 0.11]; p = .043), whereas the three-way interaction was not significant (p = .054). The results indicate that menstrual symptom frequency is associated with mental health outcomes in physically active students. Participation in the MBI was associated with changes in anxiety over time. However, the non-significant three-way interaction provided no conclusive evidence of moderation. These preliminary findings suggest potential benefits of MBI for anxiety in menstrual health context. Future studies should investigate programs that explicitly address menstrual-related aspects. This study was registered as 'Impact of an online mindfulness intervention on sleep quality in physically active students' in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the identifier DRKS00038462 on 13 November 2025. Retrospectively registered.

papers.title: Clinical and genetic landscapes of mucopolysaccharidosis type III in 20 Chinese patients.
papers.abstract: Mucopolysaccharidosis type III (MPS III), also known as Sanfilippo syndrome, is a devastating lysosomal storage disorder characterized by severe, progressive neurodegeneration. Diagnosing this condition is challenging because early somatic signs are often mild, frequently leading to misdiagnosis as autism spectrum disorder or attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder. As the subtype distribution and genetic mutation spectrum show significant ethnic heterogeneity, population-specific data are essential for accurate clinical management. This study aimed to investigate the clinical features, biochemical indicators, and genetic landscape of 20 Chinese patients (10 with type IIIA and 10 with type IIIB) to improve early recognition and diagnostic accuracy. Phenotypes and genotypes were summarized using urinary glycosaminoglycan levels, lysosomal enzyme activity assays, and whole-exome sequencing. A retrospective analysis was conducted on 20 patients with MPS III (10 with type IIIA and 10 with type IIIB). Urinary glycosaminoglycan (GAG) levels, lysosomal enzyme activities in peripheral blood leukocytes, and genetic analysis using whole-exome sequencing (WES) were performed to summarize their phenotypes and genotypes. All 20 patients exhibited progressive neurodegeneration, with initial symptoms primarily including delayed language development (100%) and cognitive regression, accompanied by varying degrees of hyperactivity, sleep disorders, and coarse facial features. Biochemical data showed the majority of patients (18/20, 90%) had significantly elevated urinary GAG excretion (with two patients showing values within normal limits), with type IIIA patients showing markedly decreased activity of heparan N-sulfatase (SGSH) and type IIIB patients showing significantly reduced α-N-acetylglucosaminidase (NAGLU) activity. Genetic testing revealed that in the SGSH gene, c.1129C>T and c.703G>A were the most frequent mutations, while in the NAGLU gene, c.1693C>T and c.1081T>C were common mutations. Compared with European populations, the proportions of IIIA and IIIB subtypes were similar in this cohort. Chinese patients with MPS III exhibit significant clinical variability and delayed diagnosis. Delayed language development accompanied by mild facial dysmorphism is an important diagnostic clue. Population-specific high-frequency mutation sites exist in the SGSH and NAGLU genes, and clarifying the mutation spectrum can aid in precise genetic counseling and prenatal diagnosis.

papers.title: Pangenome analyses reveal divergence and extensive introgression in two global corn pests.
papers.abstract: Introgression between closely related species can profoundly influence evolutionary trajectories, yet how genomic divergence interacts with introgression, especially in invasive hybridization, remains insufficiently understood. Structural variants (SVs), particularly chromosomal inversions, are key contributors to divergence and may modulate patterns of gene flow. The Asian corn borer (ACB) and European corn borer (ECB), two globally important agricultural pests, provide an excellent system to investigate these processes. We construct a graph-based pangenome from 23 high-quality genome assemblies to characterize genome-wide SVs and introgression between ACB and ECB. We identify over 216,000 SVs, most of which are associated with transposable elements and contribute to interspecific divergence. Population genomic analyses reveal widespread yet asymmetric introgression, predominantly from ACB into ECB populations in China. Introgressed regions are more prevalent in autosomes than in sex chromosomes and are enriched for genes involved in adaptive pathways. In contrast, large inversion regions on the Z chromosome exhibit strong genetic differentiation and reduced introgression, suggesting a role in maintaining species barriers. Notably, a highly divergent region containing the circadian clock gene period (per) shows signatures of selection. Functional validation using CRISPR/Cas9 demonstrates that per significantly influences diapause regulation, linking genomic divergence to adaptive phenotypic variation. Our results demonstrate that introgression and structural variation jointly shape genomic divergence in these species. While introgression facilitates the spread of adaptive variation, chromosomal inversions restrict gene flow and maintain species integrity. This study provides new insights into the evolutionary mechanisms underlying divergence, adaptation, and invasion in major agricultural pests.

papers.title: Yield of epileptiform abnormalities and predictors on routine electroencephalography in a neurology facility in Ghana.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is an essential neurodiagnostic tool for the evaluation of epilepsy and other neurological disorders. However, evidence on the yield of epileptiform abnormalities of routine EEG and its predictors in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. To determine the yield of epileptiform abnormalities of routine EEG and identify factors associated with epileptiform discharges in a Ghanaian tertiary referral centre. This study included 124 patients who underwent routine outpatient EEG between October 2023 and January 2026. Demographic, clinical, medication, and EEG characteristics were collected using a standardized data extraction form. The primary outcome was the presence of epileptiform discharges. Associations between patient characteristics and epileptiform activity were assessed using Chi-square and Fisher's exact tests. Multivariable logistic regression was performed to identify independent predictors, with results reported as adjusted odds ratios (aORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The mean age of participants was 29.4 ± 19.7 years, and 55.6% were male. Epileptiform discharges were identified in 72 patients, yielding an overall epileptiform abnormality of 58.1%. Generalized epilepsy accounted for 83.3% of epileptiform abnormalities. The highest yield was observed among children aged 0-5 years (83.3%) and adults aged ≥ 60 years (75.0%). On bivariate analysis, generalized slowing (90.9%, p = 0.025) and focal slowing (100.0%, p < 0.001) were significantly associated with epileptiform discharges. In multivariable analysis, abnormal EEG background activity remained the only independent predictor of epileptiform discharges (aOR = 23.47, 95% CI: 2.95-186.86, p = 0.003). Routine EEG demonstrated a high yield of epileptiform abnormalities in this Ghanaian tertiary centre. Abnormal EEG background activity was a strong independent predictor of epileptiform discharges, highlighting the importance of careful background assessment during EEG interpretation and supporting the continued use of routine EEG in epilepsy evaluation.

papers.title: Systematic review on the association between brain-related measures and upper limb movement characteristics after stroke.
papers.abstract: Upper limb (UL) movements are highly diverse, as are movement deficits following stroke. The relationship that stroke pathology has with UL impairments and their recovery has been studied with an increasingly complex array of neuroimaging and neurophysiology tools. This systematic review summarizes evidence on brain-related measures and UL movement in subjects with stroke. Bibliographic databases were systematically searched for combinations of 'brain function' and 'kinematics/ kinetics/ muscle activity' and 'stroke' and 'upper limb'. Studies were included if both brain and UL movement measures were assessed in at least 10 subjects. Each study was evaluated for risk of bias (adapted QUADAS-2 tool). Information on assessments for brain and UL measures, their associations, and experimental tasks was extracted, summarized, and synthesized. This study was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42025637373). A total of 220 studies were included that reported 288 experimental tasks across 4'954 subjects with stroke (mean 59.7 years). Transcranial magnetic stimulation, functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), and electroencephalography, commonly combined with grip force sensors and motion sensor- or camera-based systems, were the most frequently used methodologies. Overall, 92 brain-related and 201 UL metrics were assessed. Risk of bias was low-to-moderate. Structural brain measures revealed associations between corticospinal tract integrity and greater grip strength, as well as kinematic differences between left- and right-hemisphere stroke locations. For functional brain measures, increased activation of ipsilesional motor areas during fMRI was associated with improved smoothness. In addition, studies reported reduced activation intensity and excitability after stroke, alongside task-related recruitment of additional brain areas. This review summarizes a large and heterogeneous body of research reflecting substantial methodological and technological advances in the assessment of brain and UL movement measures after stroke. The current findings support the relevance and utility of combining brain-based and UL metrics to identify meaningful associations between neurological injury, brain function, and behavioral outcomes after stroke and thereby provide an improved understanding of movement after stroke.

papers.title: Sleep as a Modifiable Risk Factor for Progression to Substance Use Disorder: A Review of Applicability in Adolescents with Early Life Adversity.
papers.abstract: Substance use disorder (SUD) often originates in childhood and adolescence, with early life adversity (ELA) being a particularly potent risk factor increasing susceptibility. This narrative review explores the intricate relationships between ELA, sleep disturbances, and substance use in adolescents. We identified relevant articles through a PubMed search of keywords (ELA, sleep, substance use, adolescents), focusing on peer-reviewed research and reviews from the past three years, supplemented by reference list reviews and prior exposure based on previous work in the area. We examine psychological and neurobiological processes underlying ELA-induced sleep disturbances and substance use, as well as the bidirectional relationship between sleep and substance use. We also discuss the efficacy of sleep-focused interventions in improving mental health and reducing substance use, noting untested potential in ELA-exposed youth. By focusing on core but less studied pathways underlying substance use behaviors, such as internalizing psychopathology and subcortical circuits, future research can pave the way for innovative new interventions to significantly impact life trajectories in this vulnerable population.
